Inline clearance: the -32602 vocabulary gate recognised the Word-colon-detail shape by two hard-coded call-site names, so R1615's UnknownTag would have been reported dead and UnknownProposalKind had been on the wire unpublished since it was written; the rule is derived from the shape now. 20 counterfactuals, 20 caught after repair; a 45-assertion demo on the code editor, R1613's demo re-passing through the new wire as proof the question got smaller, and 19 field-bearing demos re-run for the router regression.

the wire says what a level MAY be: WireField.values plus window_declare::LEVEL_WIRE_NAMES closes debt-window-level-vocabulary-not-on-the-framework-wire, the analyzer-tool plane-C debt R1610.1's own close audit opened. Declared `api` because the deliverable is a SCHEMA capability -- a key with a closed value set now says so and says which values -- rather than a window capability; R1610 already took osnative for the level itself. THE DEFECT IS R1566's, ONE FIELD OVER. R1610.1 projected the level onto a String for two good reasons -- this crate owns the wire shape, and the axis must be parsed BEFORE any other axis in the same message is applied rather than aborting the whole frame at deserialization -- and its own carry named the cost: the earlier Option<WindowLevel> draft got serde's unknown-variant error, which LISTS the valid values, and the projection threw that away. What was left was UnknownLevel, a word telling a client its spelling was wrong and never what a right one looks like, plus level_names on one binding's own external, which is an application surface another binding need not have. Knowing that matching is safe is worthless without knowing what to match -- the exact thing R1566 fixed for error payloads, and the gate R1610 repaired while reintroducing the shape beside it. VALUES IS THE VALUE HALF OF OF, NOT A SECOND SPELLING OF IT. `of` names a censused TYPE and only a typed Rust field can carry one, because the census compares its declaration against the parsed source; a key deliberately typed String therefore has no way to reference an enum, and the closed set it accepts had nowhere to live. WireField.values is that slot, and the census describes its own new key so an agent reading rpc/schema learns the slot exists the same way it learns every other. THE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER RETYPED: LEVEL_WIRE_NAMES is a const computed in a while loop from WindowLevel::ALL, so its length is the domain census's length by construction and there is no second copy of a closed set to go stale in silence. A hand list here would have been the debt's own shape one layer down. THE PUBLISHED SET AND THE ACCEPTED SET ARE PROVEN TO BE ONE SET, which is the only thing that makes publishing worth anything: every published spelling is driven through the real window_declare parse path and must land, and a non-member must be refused by name, with the negative control asserting it is genuinely outside the set. That check lives with the axis because only the axis knows its parse path; what is general lives in the census gate -- a values declaration must sit on a string-bearing key, be non-empty, and hold distinct non-empty spellings, and at least one field must declare one, because a census slot nothing fills is a promise to a client nobody keeps. AND THE REFUSAL NOW LEADS SOMEWHERE: the -32602 entry says that a word naming a closed value set does not carry the set and that rpc/schema does, by the name of the slot. A word that leads to pinion's source is the loop this whole surface exists to end. 5 counterfactuals, 5 caught after one was found to be MISWRITTEN rather than uncaught -- it deleted the tail of the sentence and left the pointer intact, so the gate was right and the counterfactual was wrong, which is worth recording because a PASSED counterfactual is normally a finding and this one was a fixture defect. A 40-assertion demo reads the value set off rpc/schema, drives every published spelling, refuses four non-members, and round-trips a value read from scene/windows straight back into scene/window_declare -- the read and write sides speaking one vocabulary. r1610, r1576, r1539 and r1089 re-pass unchanged.

a window says WHOSE answer it is: pinion_core::display::DisplayHome plus scene/windows.display_home plus use_window_home close debt-display-home-not-cross-checked, and crates/pinion-shell/tests/winit_level_model.rs closes debt-level-support-models-a-vendored-crate -- the analyzer-tool audit's two remaining plane-C debts, both registered by R1576 and R1610's own close audits. Declared osnative because both are window-system integration, and the tool DEMANDED a re-judgment of this axis (round-axis 1 -> 3), which is recorded as 63 -> 66 below. THE DEFECT WAS A DERIVATION NOBODY CHECKED. R1576 derives a window's home from its rectangle -- the display with the largest share -- and deliberately keeps no second stored copy. The window system HAS a second answer and we never once compared them, so a divergence was not a fact this framework could hold. Measured against the window backend's own four desktop implementations rather than assumed, there are FOUR RULES: two resolve by largest intersection, one caches an answer refreshed only inside a synthetic configure path when the scale factor changes, and one reports the first compositor output the surface entered, which is not geometric at all -- and one of them answers with the FIRST ENUMERATED monitor for a window that is on no monitor, where this framework answers nowhere. So the two can differ without either being wrong, which is why this is a REPORT and not a gate: a gate would have to invent a rule overriding a platform's own. DisplayHome is five arms over the product of two options, its single constructor is the only way to build one, and its published vocabulary is proved by DRIVING that constructor over every combination and asserting set equality -- a stronger claim than a const derived from a data-less enum can make, because it pins what the code can emit rather than what the type declares. PAST THE TOOLKIT BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY ASSERTION: it has both answers too and HIDES ONE. Its geometric resolver is declared in a private header so an application cannot call it, it decides by CENTRE POINT (a window nine tenths on the right panel whose centre is on the left resolves left) with a fallback that keeps the LAST intersecting sibling it iterated, and it is consulted only when the application itself moves the window -- and even then short-circuits whenever the current screen contains the centre. A user dragging across a seam never runs it. Nothing there puts the two side by side and an application cannot, because one of them is unreachable; the public screen-at query takes a POINT, which is the rectangle-shaped gap R1576 already recorded. THE MODEL OF A VENDORED CRATE IS NOW CHECKED AGAINST IT. R1610 wrote the per-backend level table by reading the backend's source once; nothing held the two together, so the backend implementing Wayland stacking would leave our table saying unsupported forever with neither compiler nor test noticing. The gate parses every set_window_level under platform_impl with a real parser (not a regex -- R1527) and classifies each from TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS that must agree: the parameter binding is underscore-prefixed, and its identifier does not occur in the body. When they disagree it FAILS rather than guesses. The claim is therefore exact in one direction and bounded in the other, which is stated rather than papered over: every Unsupported verdict is proved to be a deliberate no-op, every Applied verdict only that the level reaches the implementation. The census is keyed by PATH and an unrecognised one fails, because a version bump that moves or adds a backend is exactly when the model needs re-reading. It also states the under-report it is making on purpose: one unnamed backend genuinely drives levels and we report Unknown for it. THE BINDING GETS THE SAME READ, because a window's screen accessor is ordinary application API in the toolkit and leaving in-process code below that while the wire is past it is the wrong asymmetry (R1576's own argument). One derivation, two callers: the view uses the hook, the oracle uses the handle it resolved at wiring time, and both funnel into one formatter. THE STAMP HAD TO MOVE TOO -- homes are stamped at window creation and on every Moved, not only at RPC dispatch, because a GUI-only session issues no dispatch and the painted readout would have shown where the window was at boot, forever. Cost checked against the backend rather than assumed: its monitor enumeration is cached behind a lock, leaving one outer-position read per window, which is what the cursor path already pays. R1616's values slot gains four more consumers: level_outcome's kind, declared and backend all carry closed sets and R1610 published none of them. 17 COUNTERFACTUALS, 17 CAUGHT, AND THE ROUND'S THREE REAL FINDINGS CAME FROM THEM. The substrate test could not tell a wholesale replacement from a merge because its only stamp was the first one, so the map was empty either way -- the handle-side twin WAS caught, which is what named the gap. Nothing checked that a published value set is what its producer emits, only that it was well-formed, so the census could retype a closed set by hand and stay green: that is R1616's own second-copy failure reintroduced inside the census, and it now has a test that drives each producer and compares. And the round's scratch driver restored with a metadata-preserving copy, so the restored file looked OLDER than the artifact built from the defect and cargo served that artifact to the next case -- the concrete form of the standing rebuild-after-revert rule, and every verdict after the first restore was void until the whole run was redone. The committed driver (R1600.1) does not have that bug and REFUSES a scoped gate, which is the other mistake the scratch run made; the final run went through it with one unscoped whole-suite gate. A 46-assertion demo, and r1576, r1610 and r1616 re-pass unchanged.

a node that paints from ONE declaration still says why: pinion_core::marks domain::NODE plus MarkSet::whole/because plus marks on Box, Path, Image and Container advance debt-assembled-state-is-published-by-one-binding, the analyzer-tool plane-A debt R1615 registered. Declared `none` because no Phase B capability moved -- this is an introspection channel reaching the nodes it had skipped, and R1615 took the text axis for the mechanism itself. THE DEBT SAID COVERAGE AND IT WAS MECHANISM. Its own file recorded that R1615 closed the mechanism and only coverage remained; measured, the mechanism reached Text and TextGrid alone, and everything the other ten bindings assemble -- a grid row, a selected cell, a dimmed port, a colour pad -- is a filled rectangle whose marks channel is Uniform, which R1615 read as having nothing to attribute. It is the opposite. "The node itself IS the run" was always a statement about the SHAPE of the attribution, not about its absence, and a rectangle's colour is routinely a composition -- selected, and hovered, and inside a collapsed group -- whose parts live in different externals. domain::NODE is that index space: one position, the node. Stated as a domain rather than as a second list on purpose, so the declaration order, the last-wins rule, the positional query and the wire form stay ONE mechanism; a caller writes because(name) and never an index, because a [0, 0) run covers nothing and would publish a reason that answers no question. THE CENSUS WAS COUNTING A DIFFERENT QUESTION, and that is the round's largest finding. The debt asks whether a widget's APPEARANCE is a function of several externals; the tool counted whether a file READS several anywhere in its source. The two come apart in both directions and both were measured: hello-row-dissect reads its second external inside apply_access_action, which runs after the picture and cannot decide it, while hello-grouped-grid and hello-grouped-list read two in read_state and then paint with view(state.selected, frame), dropping one. What makes this decidable rather than a judgment call is STRUCTURAL: WidgetCore::view(state, frame) is handed no &Scene at all, so a view cannot read an external and every path from an external to the picture runs through read_state. Reads are now bucketed by the function body they sit in, with call following to a FIXPOINT rather than one level -- the binding this census exists for reaches its second external through read_state -> read_brush -> brush(), so a one-level scan dropped the subject of the debt out of its own population, which its own selftest then caught. Every read outside that path is REPORTED under the function it sits in rather than dropped, R1605's rule. 11 -> 6, and the whole-file count is printed beside it because the difference IS the finding. A VERDICT IS NOW A THING WITH A PROOF. The debt allowed two answers for an assembling binding -- publish, or record why it need not -- and the second only with proof. Four bindings carry one: the two grouped ones because their roving cursor steers the keyboard and the accessibility tree and is never painted, and hello-selection-toolbar and settings-panel because their assembly is SPATIAL, two widgets side by side rather than one node decided by several. Each proof is behavioural and lives in that binding's own tests -- hold one external still, vary the other, assert the painted subtree is byte-identical, with a negative control asserting the other direction DOES move -- so a binding that starts painting the second contribution fails its own proof and owes the publication. The tool REFUSES a verdict whose named test is absent, and refuses one for a binding that no longer assembles. ASSEMBLE 6, PUBLISH 2, VERDICT 4, OPEN 0, and OPEN 0 is a gate rather than a number somebody reads. THE FORCING CONSUMER IS HONEST: the colour picker's saturation/value pad has its BASE from the hue slider and its THUMB from itself, so it is one painted node that is genuinely a function of two externals, and a client asking why it is that colour previously got half an answer from either and had to compose the other half -- which means reimplementing the framework's composition client-side. It also forced the sharpest design finding: that pad is a CONTAINER, and a container paints its own BoxStyle. Structural's doc claimed such a node "paints nothing of its own", which is false for the commonest shape there is, a panel with a background. So a container publishes the reasons for its own fill while its children carry their own, and the channel keeps describing where the CONTENT's attribution lives. No enum arm was added; a doc that was wrong was corrected. TWO OF R1615's OWN TESTS BECAME FALSE AND WERE REPAIRED WITHOUT LOSING THEIR TEETH: the channel derivation keyed Carries off "this kind answers Silent", which a box now does too, so it keys off WHICH INDEX SPACE the kind publishes in -- read by asking each kind to publish one reason through its own real API, a fourth independent statement that never reads marks_channel. And a plain box is now Silent rather than NoChannel: nobody asked, which stays distinct from having no channel at all. THE GATE CAUGHT THE AUTHOR TWICE. A const declaration inserted between an #[allow] and the fn it applied to silently detached it, and clippy reported the two lints that attribute had been suppressing. The settings-panel proof's first draft asserted on the font slider, which the default section does not paint, so find_with_tag answered None -- the tags were then read out of the painted scene rather than assumed. And the grouped bindings' negative control failed on correct code because source row 3 sits in a collapsed group, so the control now SEARCHES for a selection that moves the picture instead of picking one. 10 counterfactuals through the committed driver under one unscoped gate that runs the Rust suites AND the census's own tests AND the census, because four of them break a tool no cargo test can see. A 33-assertion demo, and r1615, r1613 and r709 re-pass unchanged.

the pointer wire says WHICH BUTTONS ARE HELD: PointerButtons promoted from the raw capture channel to the router's own per-pointer state, stamped onto every dispatched pointer event, closing debt-pointer-wire-omits-held-button-state and with it the Model/View axis's named blocked item, drag-select across sections. Declared `modelview` because that axis recorded the gap by name at R1562 and re-recorded it at R1563; the catalog axis was waiting on the same one item. THE DEBT FILE'S DIAGNOSIS WAS HALF WRONG AND IT COST 188 LINES. It said the type had no counterpart on the wire. The TYPE existed from R1418, lmr codec and all -- what was missing was the CHANNEL: the held set rode RawPointerButton only, which an External reaches by opting into wants_raw_pointer_buttons, so a drag-select gesture (by definition a press that leaves the pressed widget) could not see it. A duplicate type was written and then found by the lib.rs re-export and reverted. A debt that records an absence must record the AXIS of the absence or the round that opens it rebuilds what is there. THE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT THE PROMOTION FIXED: RawGrab kept its OWN copy of the set, seeded EMPTY at the grab's first press, so a raw sink grabbed while another button was already down was told that button was up. One writer, one answer, and the grab's lifetime is now read from the pointer's set rather than from a private mirror. THE RELEASE IS ITSELF AN EVENT REPORTING THE BUTTON UP, which is the round's sharpest finding and it was a real bug for an hour: the coordinator's rule "if the primary button is not held, close the gesture" sat at the top of the handler, so the release tripped it before the sweep could be consumed and EVERY drag collapsed back to one row on mouse-up. The end verdict is now TAKEN and carried down the handler. THE SECOND DEFECT THE DEBT NAMED CLOSED WITHOUT BEING WORKED ON: a release outside the window used to strand a coordinator's re-derived pressed flag forever. There is no flag now -- the state travels with the event, so whatever arrives next closes the gesture. THE WRITER IS IDEMPOTENT ON PURPOSE, so every entry point that represents a button edge notes its own without a census of which of them overlap on a given press; a list would go stale, the property does not. THE 3-TUPLE BECAME A NAMED SendPayload over 79 sites: the wire has grown a segment three times and each growth re-broke every consumer's destructuring, not because the consumer was wrong but because an anonymous tuple has no way to say a fourth fact exists and may be ignored. AN ADJACENT GAP HAD TO CLOSE TOO AND ONLY THE DEMO FOUND IT: R781 put modifiers on the RELEASE only, which held for 838 rounds because every chord-aware widget acted on the activation edge -- and stops holding the moment a gesture BEGINS at a press, because a Ctrl-anchored sweep is a function of the chord held when the finger went down. The unit test passed by feeding the payload directly; the wire could not produce it. The router now caches the shell's absolute modifier state and stamps both axes on every arm. HAND-ROLLED GRAMMAR IS NOT EXEMPT: two split_once(':') decoders broke, a test fixture and hello-scene-scale -- and the latter had ALREADY been silently inert on any Shift-click since R781. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught, but only after the driver itself was fixed: a killed first run left one file mutated (the R1617 lesson, hit again), the next run started RED, and all eight of its CAUGHT verdicts were void while the summary read 8/12. tools/counterfactual.py now runs the gate once unmutated and refuses a red baseline -- the only failure mode it had that looks like success -- with its own test. Two counterfactuals then PASSED and both were real: nothing in the Rust suite caught the press losing its chord (the demo did, which is the R1618 lesson recurring), and nothing caught the RPC read publishing a constant, because the producer sat between the router suite and the rpc suite and was reached by neither. Both now have tests. A 38-assertion demo drives the whole gesture through the ordinary pointer methods -- no drag-select RPC was invented, because a sweep IS a press and some moves and a special method would let the AI-driven gesture diverge from the physical one. 21 blast-radius demos re-pass. New debt: debt-drag-select-has-no-autoscroll (the reference's abstract item view has an auto-scroll property, an edge-margin property and a start-auto-scroll entry point; the hard part is not the timer but re-resolving hover when content moves under a stationary cursor).

a drag reaches PAST the edge: pinion_core::widgets::scroll::AutoScroll plus InputRouter::tick_auto_scroll plus scene/input_state.auto_scroll close debt-drag-select-has-no-autoscroll, the residue R1619 left one round earlier. Declared `modelview` because the item is the same one R1562 named: a sweep that can only reach what is painted is not the gesture, and every virtualized view in the tree is windowed. THE DEBT NOTE I WROTE ONE ROUND AGO WAS WRONG, AND A TEST SAID SO IN FIVE MINUTES. It claimed the hard part was re-resolving hover when content moves under a stationary cursor, and that the router had no trigger for it. Measured: it does. refresh_hover_for_all_active_pointers runs on every repaint and skips only gesture-PINNED pointers, which a plain drag-select is not -- so scrolling the content mid-sweep already extended the selection ([[0,1]] -> [[0,2]] -> [[0,3]] with the cursor untouched). That is TWO ROUNDS RUNNING where a debt note's diagnosis was false, R1619 on an inherited one and R1620 on its own, one round old. A note written at round-end without a test is a guess, and it costs the next round the time to disprove it. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was the ramp and the frame tick, and the design parts from the reference on the axis that matters. Read from its source rather than assumed: its counter starts at zero when auto-scroll begins and increments once per timer tick (capped at the page step), and THAT counter is the per-tick distance -- so the speed is a function of elapsed time alone and the pointer's depth into the margin is read as a boolean. A user who wants to go faster cannot; one who overshoots waits for the ramp to restart. Here the band IS a ramp: zero at its inner edge, the declared maximum at the boundary, linear between, saturating outside. Measured over ten identical frames through the wire: 61 px shallow versus 231 px deep. It also deletes a state -- there is no ramp counter to reset, because speed is a pure function of position. And it integrates a velocity against the frame's own dt, where the reference scrolls a fixed step per 50 or 150 ms timer tick (hard-coded, with a source comment wishing it were a style hint). NOTHING IS FABRICATED. The reference makes the selection follow the scroll by SYNTHESISING a mouse-move and posting it to the viewport, an event the application cannot tell from the user's. Here the new hover target is a derivation of the new picture, on a path that already existed -- which is why the probe above mattered: the round leaned on it and proved it first. THE PIN IS THE GESTURE. The region is captured at the press (weakly, with its viewport rect AND its declared policy) because auto-scroll's most useful moment is when the pointer is dragged PAST the edge, and at that moment a hit-test finds nothing. Pinning also makes the gesture belong to ONE region, the way its selection does. The policy is snapshotted too: a default-valued fallback would have switched a region that declared OFF back on at exactly the moment the pin starts being used. A COUNTERFACTUAL MADE THE ROUND DELETE CODE. The tick was gated on both `held_buttons(id).is_empty()` and the pin's presence, and nothing could catch removing the first -- because a pin exists exactly while a button is held, so the two could never disagree. Two readers of one fact, and the fix was to delete a check rather than to test it. Another moved the repeat/auto-scroll composition off the shell and onto the router: `a() || b()` short-circuits and would silently halve a press that is both repeating and scrolling, and the shell had no fixture that could drive both, so the composition went where the R1549 fixtures live and got the test it could not have had. tools/counterfactual.py's own R1619 baseline gate paid for itself immediately. A third found that off() zeroes BOTH the band and the speed, so no test could say which half of is_enabled was load-bearing; a zero-width band with a live speed now has one. 9 counterfactuals, 9 caught, after one was retired as mis-written (its edit was inert because the real gate sits one level down, and the property it named is covered by the pin case). The per-frame shell seam is renamed tick_pointer_hold_for_window: a second continuation arriving under a name that promised only the first is how three backends end up with two seams that drift. A 33-assertion demo drives the whole thing through the ordinary pointer methods and reads the ramp off the wire at four depths on both edges; 12 blast-radius demos re-pass including the auto-repeat one.

a display says how much of it is usable AND how sure it is: pinion_core::display::UsableRegion plus usable_regions plus the pinion-shell _NET_WORKAREA probe plus scene/displays.usable close debt-display-usable-region-unmodelled -- the last BUILDABLE analyzer-tool plane-C gap. Declared `osnative` because it is a window-system integration probe, the same axis R1617 advanced; the gated part of that axis (Mac/Win surfaces) is untouched. THE REFERENCE'S OWN SOURCE IS THE FINDING. Its X11 plugin carries an internal comment saying that deriving a per-monitor work area from the desktop-wide atom is unreliable, that window managers disagree about what the atom means with several monitors attached, and that the WM specification has no atom for the per-monitor answer. Its conclusion is the part that matters: its screen accessor RETURNS THE FULL BOUNDS for every display as soon as more than one is attached, unless an environment variable overrides -- so on any two-monitor desk it answers 'all of it is available' and the caller cannot tell that from a measurement. Two different facts arriving as one value with the difference discarded at the boundary, which is R1617's shape exactly. SO THE ANSWER CARRIES ITS PROVENANCE. Four arms, not Option<Rect>: reported (a measurement), desktop_wide (a work area exists but this desk has several displays and the clip cannot be attributed), unpublished (the platform has none -- Wayland, where the protocol does not tell a client), unprobed (nobody asked). `rect()` answers on every arm so a client placing a window never matches; `is_measured()` is true only for the first. Option<Rect> would have fused 'no panels', 'cannot say' and 'nobody looked' into one absence. AND THE DERIVATION RECOVERS DISPLAYS THE REFERENCE GIVES UP ON. If the desktop work area takes NOTHING from a display, that display's whole bounds are usable and that is a real answer however many displays the desk has -- so a dock down the left monitor leaves the right monitor with a measurement, where the reference loses both. Only the displays the atom actually clips are unattributable. A display the work area misses entirely reports its bounds rather than an empty rect, because 'none of this display can be used' is the one answer certainly wrong. THE PROBE IS REAL AND IT RAN. x11rb was already in the tree transitively via winit, so the dependency is a direct edge rather than a second copy, and it is target-scoped. Measured on this desk through the wire: usable 2494x1568+66+32, reported -- a 66px left dock and a 32px top bar, off the live root window. A Wayland session is refused BEFORE connecting, because under XWayland the atom describes the X root rather than the compositor's panels and answering would be a guess about the wrong desk. Every failure inside the probe collapses to None on purpose: a work area is an optimisation on placement, and a shell that refused to start over a missing property would trade a cosmetic answer for the application. THREE COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED FIRST AND ALL THREE WERE REAL. Nothing caught 'probed-and-empty' collapsing into 'never probed' -- the distinction the type exists for. Nothing caught the wire publishing a constant provenance, and nothing caught the schema's closed value set being hand-written instead of derived from the arms; the demo could catch neither, because a real desk produces one arm out of four. All three now have tests, and the schema test asserts the DECLARED set equals the set the conversion can emit. 10 counterfactuals, 10 caught, from a verified-green baseline. The wire type is declared in pinion-rpc rather than core (the DisplayHomeWire precedent -- the census that keeps rpc/schema honest reads only that crate), and the value set is R1616's `values` slot fed from UsableRegion::WIRE_NAMES, a const derived from the arms. A 20-assertion demo reads the vocabulary off rpc/schema before parsing, checks the region never exceeds its bounds, and asserts the declared set is strictly larger than what this desk produced -- because a single-arm enum would make the provenance decorative. 5 display-family demos re-pass.

the crate stacks: pinion_chart::stack + StackedBand + stacked_value_bounds + draw::area_between + LineChart::stacked pay the chart residue's plainest item -- the crate drew several areas over one another and left the ACCUMULATION to the application. A binding wanting a stacked area chart had to hand in a series whose y was already a running sum, so the chart's tooltips, legend and value axis all reported the TOTAL where the reader sees a band, and the original measurement was gone before anything could ask. That is the shape the standing directive rules out: the deliverable is a crate that composes. THE AUDIT CAME FIRST, BECAUSE THE DEBT FILE DEMANDED IT, AND IT MOVED THE LIST. The file's own How-to-apply says every item is an R1568 judgment to re-check against the code, since its #1-#7 all went stale that way. Measured: the CATEGORY AXIS IS PRESENT (TickFormat::Category(Categories) in ticks.rs) -- that entry was stale. LABEL THINNING exists in some form (a whole-decade stride). LOCAL TIME is absent BY STATED DESIGN, with civil.rs saying it needs a timezone database, which makes it an external dependency rather than a gap. And the per-mark a11y item is MIS-FRAMED: it names box/candle/polar as lacking what others have, but the whole crate has no AccessNode at all, so that is one axis-wide question and not three widget ones. Genuinely absent and correctly framed: OHLC, spline, stacked area, violin, and SVG `d` / Arc-Quad -- and the last of those is a Scene::Path vocabulary axis the file itself says is not really dataviz. STACKING IS TWO CURVES, NOT ONE, which is why area_path could not express it: it closes onto a SCALAR baseline. area_between walks the upper curve forwards and the lower backwards so the ring closes without a bow tie where a negative series crosses. And the band keeps both facts -- Series::points is what was measured, upper/lower is where it is drawn -- so nothing has to reconstruct one from the other. IT REFUSES TO GUESS. Stacking is only defined on a shared x grid: adding a value sampled at 10:00 to one sampled at 10:07 requires deciding what the second was doing at 10:00, and every answer is an interpolation the chart would be inventing. A series whose grid disagrees is drawn UNSTACKED on the baseline rather than resampled, because a picture whose totals are not the data's totals is the one failure a stacked chart must not have. The f64 grid comparison is exact on purpose and says so: these are the same numbers the caller put in, so a tolerance would only admit a genuinely different grid. Negatives stack DOWNWARD from the running total rather than being clamped. A hidden series contributes nothing and draws no band, while the ones above keep their palette index, so a legend toggle re-stacks without re-colouring. THE AXIS DEFECT IS THE ONE A CALLER MEETS FIRST: three series each peaking at 40 reach 120, and a plot scaled to the per-series maximum clips two thirds of the picture. stacked_value_bounds is its own function for that reason, and resolved_y_domain was EXTRACTED from build_body because a counterfactual proved the choice untestable inline -- a test can compare two pictures but cannot say which domain produced either. That extraction is the round's second finding-driven structural change. 8 counterfactuals, 8 caught, from a verified-green baseline; two were rewritten after cargo fmt moved their anchors and one after it did not compile. A 14-assertion demo drives the real binary: hello-chart-fill is now stacked (an area chart of several series is FOR the total), and the demo asserts the bands do not share a baseline -- which overlapping areas necessarily do -- and that they differ in height, so a single merged silhouette would fail. The value axis's extent is checked in Rust rather than in the demo, because reading it back off painted tick text compares an SI-rounded string to a float and would pass for the wrong reason. 3 chart-family demos re-pass.

a path keeps the curve it was authored as: pinion_core::path_data plus PathCommand::QuadTo / ArcTo plus the closed PathSegment form close the analyzer-tool audit's `SVG d parsing / Arc-Quad commands` row -- the last of the chart-residue items that is not a series type, and the one the debt file itself said is really a Scene::Path VOCABULARY axis rather than dataviz. Declared `none` rather than an axis for that reason: no Phase B capability moved, this is the primitive under charting, the catalog and the DCC widgets alike, and crediting one of them would inflate an axis for work it is not named for (R1542's rule, R1606 and R1613's precedent). THE VOCABULARY SURVIVES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. The reference converts on the way IN -- quadTo computes the equivalent cubic and calls cubicTo, arcTo appends Beziers, and the stored element list has four kinds with no arc among them -- so a path there cannot be asked whether it holds a circle, and there is no inverse back to path data. Under 2#7 the scene is what a client READS, so an answer already expanded into a rasterizer's Beziers answers a different question. QuadTo and ArcTo therefore reach the scene, the wire and back out through write(), and the cubic expansion is derived on demand. WHAT IS SHORTHAND IS NOT VOCABULARY, and the line is stated: relative commands, H/V and the smooth S/T are fully determined by what precedes them and are resolved at parse time; a quadratic's DEGREE and an arc's ellipse are not, so those two are kept. THE ENUM COULD NOT GROW SAFELY BEFORE THIS. PathCommand is non_exhaustive and every consumer matched it with a wildcard, so a new arm would have been skipped by the Vello adapter (`_ => {}`) and collapsed to `"Unknown"` on the wire -- painting nothing and introspecting as nothing, with nothing failing. The answer is a second CLOSED type: PathSegment is not non_exhaustive and the only way to obtain one is for_each_segment, whose match is exhaustive inside pinion-core where non_exhaustive does not apply. The wire is closed the same way, by rendering PathCommand::describe's three argument shapes instead of the commands themselves, which is what let the Unknown arm be DELETED rather than extended. The paint hash follows describe too, and that is the arm that mattered most: a hand-written hasher that forgot the sweep flag would give the two halves of a circle ONE hash and the fragment cache would paint one with the other's pixels. THE ERROR CHANNEL IS THE OTHER HALF. The reference's parser answers std::nullopt -- one bit, no position, no cause -- and is unreachable anyway, declared only in private headers, so every application writes its own. Three of its behaviours are silent acceptances rather than errors, each now a named test: data that does not begin with a moveto (it seeds MoveTo(0,0) through ensureData and draws from the origin), a trailing letter with no arguments (the argument array comes back empty, the loop body never runs, and the command vanishes with the path reported valid), and a non-finite number (parsed to infinity, then lineTo/cubicTo bail on !hasValidCoords, warning only in debug builds). Here each is a PathDataError carrying the byte offset, the command letter and the cause. Empty `d` parses to an empty path, which is what SVG says and what the reference calls failure. A COUNTERFACTUAL FOUND A REAL HOLE IN THE ROUND'S OWN TESTS. Replacing F.6.5.2's sign rule `large_arc == sweep` with `large_arc` alone was caught by NOTHING: the arc tests exercised sweep 0/1 at large_arc 0 and large_arc 0/1 at sweep 1, so two of the four flag pairs were never asked, and the sweep test's assertion survived a centre flip. The rule is a statement about all four pairs, so the property is now the pairing itself -- the agreeing pairs share one circle and the differing pairs share the other, with both centres computed in the test from the chord rather than read back out of the code. Cross-checked against the reference's own conversion, which carries the identical rule, so two independent implementations of F.6.5 agree and the defect was the test rather than the code. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught after that repair, from a verified-green baseline; three were re-authored because their first form did not compile and so tested nothing. The osnative axis was re-judged 66 -> 69 as the push gate demanded (R1621 moved its evidence past the band): it closes exactly one of the two platform probes R1617 named, and the gate -- Mac/Win native surfaces -- is untouched. 48 path_data tests, a paint-hash test that varies every argument of every command, an RPC census over PathCommandKind::ALL with a fixture per kind, and hello-svg-path importing four real icon `d` strings with a Toggle that swaps in malformed data so the binding REPORTS the byte instead of drawing nothing. A 60-plus-assertion demo drives the real window; r721_path, three chart demos and the donut demo re-pass unchanged.

one datum, two marks: pinion_chart::SessionMark plus CandlestickChart::with_mark adds the open-high-low-close BAR, which the chart residue named as the cheapest of its three remaining series types and which is cheap for a reason worth stating -- a candlestick and a bar are two RENDERINGS of the same four prices, so the deliverable is a mark on the chart that already exists rather than a second chart type. Declared `dataviz`: this is a series form the axis was judged short on. THE REFERENCE HAS NO BAR SERIES AT ALL, only a candlestick one, so there is nothing there for a bar to be a second series OF -- and its candlestick series is in the module that is separately licensed and absent from this machine's install. Here the sort, both x-axis readings, the logarithmic value axis and its off-scale report, the window, the inspect readout and the published direction contrast are all SHARED, because the mark is a property of the chart. A unit test asserts that: the painted session centres are identical under both marks. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT TEST WAS THE WRONG TEST, AND A COUNTERFACTUAL SAID SO. It compared `center_px` under the two marks, which is upstream of everything a mark touches, so nudging the slot geometry two pixels for bars only was caught by nothing -- no assertion in the round had looked at a painted node's position. It reads the scene now. That is the same shape as R1622's finding and the fifth round running where a passed counterfactual was a real discovery. THE PLACEMENT RULE WAS ALSO WRONG FIRST, and the fixture is what proved it. The bar was written as `the spine is the anchor, the ticks are optional', by analogy with the candle whose wicks hang off its body. Measured: on a logarithmic axis an unplaceable OPEN implies an unplaceable LOW, because the low is at or below the open -- so that case cannot happen, and the case that does happen is the reverse, where a bar with an anchor would have drawn nothing exactly where it has the most to say. A bar has NO single anchor: spine, open tick and close tick are each placed from the prices they need, so it draws whatever the axis can carry and `off_scale` names the rest. Nothing is ever clamped onto the plot floor, because a mark at an invented pixel is a price where no price is. AND THE INSPECT RING TEST FAILED FOR A THIRD REASON, WHICH WAS ALSO A FIXTURE: it focused the week fixture's middle session, which opens at its low and closes at its high, so its body IS its range and both rings measured 69 pixels whatever the code did. A session whose body is strictly inside its range is the only one that can tell a body-shaped ring from a range-shaped one. `mark_bounds` is the one place the question `where is this session drawn' is answered, so the ring and the marks cannot drift. DIRECTION SURVIVES THE LOSS OF HUE BY SHAPE. The candle answers with its body fill (the traditional Japanese form, which predates colour); a bar has no body, so it answers with the ticks -- open to the LEFT, close to the RIGHT, and on a rise the right one is higher. Asserted with every direction colour forced to one ink, so a check that passed on colour cannot pass. The binding's `no hue' chip makes that visible and the demo reads it off the painted geometry. `slot_geometry` was extracted because the two marks need the horizontal extent at different moments -- a candle only once the axis has placed its body, a bar before the axis has placed anything -- and the binding's three option toggles are now one declared list, because R1624 adding the third revealed the two hand-written copies (the keymap and the accessibility count) that made it a three-site edit. 6 counterfactuals, 6 caught after the two repairs, from a verified-green baseline. A 40-plus-assertion demo drives the real binary through both marks and back; the R1567 demo re-passes unchanged.

a smooth line says what it invented: pinion_chart::Interpolation plus LineChart::interpolation and LineChart::overshoot pay the chart residue's spline item, and the design is the report rather than the curve. Declared `dataviz`. A CHART THAT JOINS ITS SAMPLES WITH STRAIGHT LINES DRAWS ONLY VALUES THE DATA CONTAINS; A SPLINE DOES NOT. A cubic through a plateau followed by a rise dips BELOW the plateau, so a chart of a quantity that cannot be negative paints a negative anyway and nothing in the picture says so. The reference toolkit's spline series is exactly that: one method, no choice of it, its control points internal, no report. So the vocabulary here is a DECLARED choice of three -- straight, Fritsch-Carlson monotone (smooth and provably inside its own endpoints), and Catmull-Rom (smoother and free to overshoot, offered because refusing would only move the hand-rolled copy into the application) -- and `overshoot` names every segment whose curve leaves the range its own samples span, in DATA space, depending on nothing but the samples and the interpolation, the same contract off_scale has. Measured through the wire on the demo's real data: catmull-rom leaves its samples in 14 segments, worst by 42.46; monotone in none. THE GUARANTEE IS TESTED, NOT ASSERTED. `may_overshoot` is a declaration on the enum and the tests hold it to the geometry over forty pseudo-random shapes, because an interpolation that promised it could not invent a value and then did would be the worst failure available -- the promise is the whole reason to choose it. The extrema are SOLVED rather than sampled, through R1623's path bounds, so a bulge between two samples cannot be stepped over; R1623 is load-bearing here twice, since the curve is emitted as real cubic commands rather than a densely sampled polyline and a client reading the scene can tell those apart. A NON-GRAPH SERIES IS NOT SMOOTHED. A spline through samples is a function of x; a series whose x turns back is a path, and running it through a function interpolant produces a shape that is not the caller's data. It is drawn straight and `is_graph` says so, rather than silently. THE ROUND SHIPPED A DEAD CONTROL AND THE DEMO CAUGHT IT. `toggle_group::extra_toggles` drops its first tag, because in a binding's FIRST group that tag is already the primary external -- so calling it for a SECOND group produced a chip that was painted, focusable, announced to assistive technology and wired to nothing. The substrate now names the two forms apart (`toggles` keeps every tag) and both have a test; the binding has one asserting that every tag it paints has an external behind it, which is the invariant rather than the instance. A counterfactual is what demanded that test: reverting the fix was caught by the demo and by NOTHING in cargo test, and demos do not gate a push. AND THE BLAST-RADIUS SWEEP CAUGHT A SECOND ONE: feeding the keymap the merged tag list made ArrowRight wrap out of the legend and into the interpolation chips. An arrow key roves within a GROUP, and these are two groups, so the keymap asks them in turn while the census reads the merged list -- two different questions over one set of tags. 13 interpolation tests, 2 chart tests, 3 binding tests, 1 substrate test. 7 counterfactuals, 7 caught after the repair, from a verified-green baseline. A 25-assertion demo drives the real binary through all three interpolations and reads the report off both the painted caption and the live region; the R1379 demo re-passes.

the outline is an estimate, the box is the data: pinion_chart::Density plus DistributionMark and ViolinScale close the chart residue's LAST buildable item, which is also the last buildable row of the analyzer-tool audit. Declared `dataviz`. A BOX PLOT'S FIVE NUMBERS ARE ORDER STATISTICS -- every one is a value the data actually took. A VIOLIN'S OUTLINE IS NOT. It is a kernel density estimate, and the kernel, the bandwidth and the width scaling are all choices a reader cannot recover from the picture. So the estimate is a VALUE that carries them: Density publishes its kernel, its resolved bandwidth, the sample count behind it, and `spill` -- the share of the estimated mass that landed outside the range the samples actually spanned. That is R1625's question one round later and in the place it bites hardest: a Gaussian kernel has infinite support, so a violin of a quantity that cannot be negative shows density below zero unless something stops it. `Density::bounded` is that something, and it REFLECTS at the observed extremes rather than clipping, so the outline still integrates to one and spill becomes zero rather than merely hidden. A VIOLIN NEEDS A DENSITY AND A DENSITY NEEDS SAMPLES. The reference toolkit's box-set contract is five pre-computed doubles, and this crate's `from_summary` is the same shape -- so `with_density` REFUSES a summary-sourced distribution, because an estimate arriving beside five numbers that never were samples describes some other data. Such a category keeps its box under a violin mark and `without_density` names it, because the blank slot is the one answer certainly wrong: it reads as `no data` when the truth is `summarised upstream`. `from_samples_with_density` exists so the summary and the estimate cannot describe different data -- composing the two constructors takes the sample slice twice and nothing would notice a mismatch. THE WIDTH SCALING IS NOT COSMETIC. Every density integrates to one, so Width says compare the shapes, Area says compare the distributions, and Count weights by sample count -- which is the only one that lets a violin resting on twenty samples look different from one resting on four hundred. An outline hides that completely otherwise. THREE COUNTERFACTUALS PASSED AND ALL THREE WERE REAL. Nothing caught replacing the per-point width with a CONSTANT -- symmetry, containment and the scaling comparison all survive a bar, because all three ask about the outline's extremes rather than its profile; the test now asserts the profile, including that the widest point sits where the density peaks. Nothing caught dropping Silverman's robust spread, because the first test compared Silverman against Scott and the two also differ by a constant factor, so the rule stayed narrower while becoming exactly as fragile; the property is how little the bandwidth MOVES when one outlier arrives, measured at 1.48 against Scott's 35.0 and asserted either side of that gap rather than at a guessed number. And the demo's first draft demanded every violin be strictly taller than its box, which is false for a tightly clustered endpoint whose bandwidth rounds to nothing -- the estimate telling the truth, not a defect -- so it asserts containment everywhere and the bulge at least once. R1625's `toggle_group::toggles` FOUND ITS THIRD CONSUMER IMMEDIATELY: hello-boxplot had hand-rolled around `extra_toggles` skipping its first tag, with a comment saying so, and that hand-rolling is now gone. The crate's f64-to-f32 narrowing was lifted to one definition at the same time; R1625 had made a private second copy and this round would have made a third. 8 counterfactuals, 8 caught after the repairs, from a verified-green baseline. 10 density tests, 7 chart tests, 3 binding tests. A 30-plus-assertion demo drives the real binary; the R1553, R1624 and R1625 demos re-pass.

the red was not a flake: the stop-the-line gate refused to publish R1623-R1626 onto a red base, and NOT ONE of the five failures was a flake. Declared `none`: this is a stop-the-line clearance, and no Phase B capability moved. R754's PAGINATION CHEVRONS WERE DEAD. Bisected with release builds: R1618 green, R1619 red. `drive_chevron` read everything after `"prev:"` as the event name, so when R1619 grew the send wire by a fourth segment the remainder became `PointerDown::l`, `ButtonEvent::from_name` answered None, and both chevrons stopped responding entirely. Proven through the wire rather than read: a two-segment payload steps 2 -> 1 and the same payload with a buttons segment does not. Pagination was the ONLY widget hand-rolling the `:` split, and it hand-rolled because the SSOT parser's typed form assumed a numeric key -- a named key is now as first-class as a numeric one, so the reason to hand-roll is gone. AND THE DEMO'S OWN NO-OP ASSERTION WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON: `next on the last page clamps` was true because next did nothing EVER. A no-op assertion cannot tell a clamp from a corpse, so it is now paired with clicks in the direction that must move, ordered so the moving one runs first. THREE DEMOS HAND-WROTE THE WIRE'S AXIS SET and demanded set equality; R1619 added held_pointer_buttons and R1620 added auto_scroll, so all three went red for five rounds. TWO things were wrong. The census belonged in the crate that owns the emitter, because nothing makes a Python list and a Rust json! literal land in the same diff -- `INPUT_STATE_AXES` is now beside the builder and a test holds the two together in BOTH directions, a missing axis being a wire regression and an extra one a stale census. And set equality was the wrong assertion for a reader that uses four of the axes: an ADDITIVE wire change must not break a consumer that never looked at the new field, so each demo now names the axes it reads. R1182 WAS NEVER A FLAKE, AND MEMORY HAD CARRIED IT AS ONE FOR EIGHT ROUNDS. Five consecutive runs fail with the identical message. Its section H asserted that a marquee drag at the rim never auto-pans, which was a statement about what EXISTED -- there was no auto-scroll substrate -- frozen into a requirement. R1620 built one, defaulting on. Measured which of the two is right instead of restoring the old number: `use_marquee_rect` holds the band in GRAPH units, so panning under a live marquee leaves the anchor where the user put it and the band grows over ground that scrolled into view. A node starting off screen at x=700 is selected after the viewport pans 0 -> 257, which the old behaviour could not reach at all. The section now asserts that capability, including that the anchor did not drift. The lesson the round is named for: a `flake` label that has not been re-measured is not a diagnosis. The process gap is unchanged and stated -- the demo sweep does not gate a push, and R1495's CI-red stop-the-line caught this eight rounds late rather than at the round that caused it.

a fill is the same shape as its line: draw::area_path / area_path_along_x / area_between all take the Interpolation, and Density::estimate takes a DensitySpec. Declared `dataviz`. Both debts this round pays were created BY the two rounds before it, which is what obligation 3 is for. R1625 MOVED THE SERIES STROKE ONTO THE CURVE AND LEFT EVERY FILL ON THE POLYLINE, so a filled smooth chart drew a curved line over a straight-edged fill -- one node's two halves derived from different shapes, the general form of debt-paint-and-gesture-read-two-facts. A stacked band is the hard case and the reason this needed a new primitive: reversing the lower point list and re-interpolating does not work, because a DESCENDING x is not a graph, so it would fall back to straight segments and flatten the band's underside while the top stayed curved. `interpolate::append_reversed` retraces the FORWARD curve exactly instead -- a cubic from p to q with controls (c1, c2) is the same curve as one from q to p with (c2, c1) -- so no new tangent is chosen and the two edges of a band cannot disagree about the curve they share. Asserted by sampling both directions at matching parameters. AND IT CAUGHT A WIRE REGRESSION IT WAS ABOUT TO SHIP: `interpolate::commands` expressed even Interpolation::Linear as cubics, because `curve` answers in one shape for the callers that MEASURE it -- so every pre-existing filled chart's command stream would have changed from LineTo to CurveTo. The scene is a different audience: under 2#7 a client reads what was authored, and a straight segment authored straight must not arrive claiming to be a curve. A straight join now publishes as LineTo, which also leaves every existing chart byte-unchanged. The area's bbox is resolved from the CURVE rather than from the samples, since a smooth interpolation may leave the box its points span. R1626 SHIPPED Density::bounded(&self, samples), WHICH TOOK THE SAMPLE SLICE A SECOND TIME -- the exact mismatch the same round created from_samples_with_density to prevent, and nothing could have noticed a different slice, because a reflected estimate of other data looks entirely plausible. Reflecting the kernel is a RE-ESTIMATION rather than something done to an estimate afterwards, so it belongs where the estimate is decided: DensitySpec carries the kernel, the rule, the bounded choice and the resolution as one value, Density::estimate is the only constructor, and the old method is deleted. Gathering the knobs also stops the call sites growing an argument each time a fifth appears. hello-chart-fill's stack is now monotone, which is where a stack most wants a curve and where the choice is least arguable -- a stacked area chart of a sampled quantity reads as bins with straight edges, and the monotone interpolant is the one that cannot draw a total the data never reached. The R1622 demo asserts that EVERY band curves on both edges, and found something worth stating: the bottom band is drawn between two curves too, because `stack` gives it the zero line as its lower SERIES rather than a scalar baseline, which is what makes the whole stack one shape. An inert assertion was removed rather than left: the first draft checked the fill in the R1625 demo, whose binding has no fill at all, so it never ran -- a dead assertion is worse than none because it reads as coverage. clippy::too_many_lines fired on series_layer once all three area shapes took the interpolation, and `area_for` is the extraction it asked for. 4 new tests, 6 counterfactuals, 6 caught, from a verified-green baseline; 5 chart demos re-pass.

a chart says what it derived: pinion_core::derivation (the channel) plus pinion_chart::derivations (the vocabulary) plus scene/derivations close debt-chart-derivations-are-not-on-the-wire and debt-candle-caps-are-dead-under-the-bar-mark. Declared `dataviz` because the capability is a chart one: ten chart builders now state how their drawing relates to the data and the request behind it, and the reference's chart module has no analogue at any layer. THE FOUR KINDS ARE A CLOSED 2x2 rather than a list -- {data, request} x {the picture has more, the source has more} -- so invented / omitted / chosen / discarded is complete by construction and a client's match on it stays exhaustive; that is why DerivationKind is a plain enum where Evidence, whose arms are SHAPES of answer, is non_exhaustive. THE REPORTS ALREADY EXISTED AND THE PRIMARY CLIENT COULD NOT REACH THEM: LineChart::overshoot, Density's kernel / bandwidth / spill, BoxPlotChart::without_density were in-process Rust, and an RPC client holds a Scene and no chart, so under 2#2 the strongest reports in the crate were invisible to the reader they were written for. TWO RULES KEEP THE REPORT HONEST: a Chosen entry is always published (a control that only appears once it has misbehaved is not a control), and an Invented / Omitted / Discarded entry exists exactly when there is something to report -- publishing spill=0 would make 'did this chart invent anything' answer yes for every violin ever drawn. And one entry per (name, subject), never per datum: a scatter with 10,000 off-scale points publishes one count per series. THE DEAD CAPS CONTROL IS CLOSED BY REPORTING RATHER THAN DRAWING: with_caps(true) under the OHLC mark added no node and said nothing, and the bar's own open and close ticks already play the caps' role, so the honest answer is a Discarded entry naming the mark that made the setting meaningless. WITHOUT_DENSITY IS NOW KEYED OFF THE REQUEST, not the data: under a box mark no violin was asked for, so nothing was discarded -- the data-only report fires there and would have told a caller its code was wrong when it was not. THE WRITER REMOVES THE CENSUS: every chart reaches the scene through derivations::chart_root, which TAKES the set rather than defaulting it, so a chart added later cannot compile without deciding what it derived; the five charts with no report pass an empty set, which is Published-with-no-entries and a different answer from Silent. THE CHANNEL IS ON THE COMPOSITION: SceneNodeKind::derives_channel is exhaustive with four arms, and the scene test derives every expectation from an independent observable -- how many of two offered children a kind's own constructor accepts, whether an opaque-handle walk resolves it, whether the kind has a tag field at all -- never from the declaration, which is the trap the marks sibling recorded. THE ERROR VOCABULARY GATE CAUGHT THE ROUND: UnknownDerivationKind reached the wire unpublished and rpc/errors' own test refused it. 60-plus-assertion demo across three examples driving the real wire; five chart demos re-pass unchanged.

a vocabulary counts its own arms: `#[derive(VariantCensus)]` plus its application to all EIGHTEEN hand-written `ALL` lists, plus the two closures it enables -- debt-a-new-path-command-may-reuse-a-kind and debt-evidence-shape-falls-through-on-the-wire. Declared `none`: this is a soundness gate and two debt closures, and no Phase B capability moved. Crediting an axis for a gate would be the R1542 inflation R1606, R1613, R1614, R1618 and R1623 each refused. THE SHAPE IS CARRIED EIGHTEEN TIMES. An enum that publishes a vocabulary writes `pub const ALL: [Self; N]` beside itself and every consumer that must cover the vocabulary iterates it; nothing connects that list to the definition, so adding a variant and forgetting the const leaves every such consumer silently covering one fewer case while the code compiles and the tests pass. It is the `#[non_exhaustive]` wildcard moved one line down. The list cannot be REPLACED -- a variant with a payload cannot appear in a value list at all -- so the derive publishes the one fact only the definition knows (`ARMS`, `ARM_NAMES`) and `#[variant_census(all)]` asserts the length in a `const` block, so a stale list is a BUILD failure with no run to forget. Measured: none of the eighteen was stale, which is the honest result -- this is a ratchet, not a bug find. THE PATH DEBT IS CLOSED BY A CARDINALITY ARGUMENT, not by a census the language cannot express: `kind()` is TOTAL by the compiler (exhaustive inside pinion-core), the existing fixture test proves it SURJECTIVE (every kind has a command), and a total surjective map between finite sets of equal size is INJECTIVE -- so the only missing fact was the size of a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum whose arms cannot be enumerated from outside, and the derive reads it off the definition. Two commands can no longer share a wire `type`. THE EVIDENCE DEBT IS CLOSED BY R1623's OWN RECIPE: `Evidence::describe` projects onto `EvidenceForm`, a closed type obtainable no other way, so the serializer one crate over matches exhaustively and its `_ => {}` is DELETED rather than extended. Its own debt file said the value representation would be a guess; it is not -- the four forms already exist and a fifth `Evidence` arm must either map onto one (a duration is a real) or add a form, which breaks every consumer loudly. AND THE MAP IS DELIBERATELY NOT INJECTIVE, which is the asymmetry with `PathCommandKind` and is now a test: there the kind IS the command's identity so sharing one is a defect, here a form is the SHAPE of a value so sharing one is correct. THE DEMO CHECKS THE END A BUILD GATE CANNOT REACH: `rpc/schema` publishes the accepted set for four fields, and the demo reads those sets OFF THE WIRE (a hard-coded copy here would be a fifth copy of the closed set) and asserts BOTH directions -- every observed value is promised, and every promised value is produced by a real surface in the run. Neither alone is enough: soundness passes trivially against an over-long list and reachability against an under-long one. All four channel arms are reached from real surfaces, `opaque` through the STATE scene because that is where an External lives. And every evidence object is checked to carry a payload, which is the exact signature of the fallthrough this round removed. THE ROUND'S OWN FIXTURE REPRODUCED R1629's CF-5 ONE DAY LATER: the derive test's ordering assertion used First / Second / Third, which sort into their own declaration order, so it could not fail. Renamed to Zebra / Apple / Mango. The `all` assertion is compile-time and this tree has no compile-fail harness, so its firing is proven by two recorded probes (shortening `DerivationKind::ALL` and `Kernel::ALL`, in two different crates) rather than by a standing test -- stated as a limit and registered. 37-assertion demo over three examples; six counterfactuals.

eleven commands are three parameters: pinion_node_graph::arrange (Align / Distribute / Stack / Straighten over Axis x Edge) closes the ALIGNMENT cluster, the largest single block the node-graph campaign had open and the one its entry file named as the next round's first candidate. Declared `dcc`: the node graph is one of that axis's three named families and this is a capability it did not have. THE REFERENCE SPELLS ITS ARGUMENTS INTO ELEVEN NAMES -- AlignNodesLeft, AlignNodesTop, DistributeNodesHorizontally -- so the set cannot be enumerated, stored, or offered by a generic control, and every consumer writes the eleven-way match again. Here they are an axis (2), an edge (3) and a gap: six aligns, two distributes, two stacks and a straighten. TWELVE, not eleven -- ours takes the axis on Straighten too, so a top-to-bottom editor gets the command the reference's one-way graphs never needed. THREE PLACES PAST THE REFERENCE. (1) The result is a VALUE: every pass answers the same `Placement` the Sugiyama and organic passes answer, so an arrangement can be previewed, diffed or refused before anything moves, where the reference's commands write straight into the graph. (2) The stack's padding is a PARAMETER; the reference compiles a constant into the editor, so an application whose cards are twice as tall cannot ask for a proportionate gap -- the demo drives three gaps through one command and reads the clear space back off the painted scene. (3) STRAIGHTEN SAYS WHAT IT COULD NOT STRAIGHTEN: a fan-in cannot be made straight (two producers both want the consumer's free-axis coordinate) and the reference moves what it can, silently. `Straightened::bent` names every leftover link, which is the difference between 'this is as straight as it goes' and 'this tool is unreliable' -- and it is a fact about the GRAPH, so a caller can split the selection instead of pressing again. A PLACEMENT COULD NOT BE APPLIED, which the round found by needing to: the signature example wrote the write-back loop twice and this crate's own tests were about to write a third, so `Document::apply` is the rule-of-three lift. It counts only the nodes that actually moved, which is what lets an undo stack skip an empty entry -- and that count is what the wire verb answers. THE CENSUS PIN MOVED WITH PROOFS: eleven engine verdicts go absent -> have, each naming the test that exercises it through the public API (R1602's standing rule), taking GraphEditor 20/51 -> 31/51 and the engine tree 40% -> 45%. AND THE DEMO'S OWN DISTRIBUTE FIXTURE COULD NOT DISCRIMINATE at first: packing to a constant gap and then distributing reproduces the same gaps whatever the pass does, so the check would have passed against a no-op. Made uneven first, with a guard asserting it IS uneven -- the third consecutive round in which a fixture failed to distinguish the thing it was written to distinguish. 33-assertion demo reading positions off the painted scene rather than the model.

a port count is a property of the NODE, not of its kind: NodeKind::variadic declares that one run of a kind's ports repeats, Node::items carries that node's, and Document::insert_item / remove_item / move_item are the reference's FOURTEEN variadic-pin commands as two operations and a position (the engine's AddExecutionPin / InsertExecutionPinBefore / After / RemoveExecutionPin / AddOptionPin / RemoveOptionPin / SoundCueGraph::AddInput / DeleteInput / AnimGraph::AddBlendListPin / RemoveBlendListPin plus the DCC's socket_items add / remove-by-index / remove-active / move). Declared `dcc` -- it is the node-graph third of that axis, whose engine census went 45% -> 51% and GraphEditor 31/51 -> 37/51 on 17 verdicts, each with its own proof. THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY IS RE-INDEXING, and the reference ships it unfixed: UAnimGraphNode_BlendListByInt::RemovePinFromBlendList carries //@TODO: ANIMREFACTOR: Need to handle moving pins below up correctly at 5.8.1. A Socket addresses a port BY INDEX, so removing one item moves every link and every authored value after it -- including the FIXED ports past the run, which have no visual cue on the node at all -- so all three operations state only what they are (an insert, a removal, a permutation) over ITEM ORDINALS and one derivation turns that into the port map, which drives links and values together because a link kept while its value is dropped is silent corruption. That pairing is why remap_ports is lifted out of set_kind: not a count of copies but a single source for an invariant, the same argument Document::signature's own doc makes. PAST THE REFERENCES IN FOUR PLACES: the removal NAMES the wires it cut and hands back the values it dropped (the reference answers void after BreakAllPinLinks); one declaration fixes place, template, floor and ceiling so 'may I remove one' and 'what happens when I do' cannot disagree (the reference spreads them over CanAddPin, a per-class CanRemoveExecutionPin, a per-class GetPinNameGivenIndex and a RemoveInputPin whose interface DEFAULT IS AN EMPTY BODY); the ordinal is applied when the signature RESOLVES so a name can never be stale and there is no 'Z'-'A' arity ceiling (that limit exists because the reference NAMES its pins for the letters); and an Item may carry its own name and socket type, which is what all but one of the DCC's socket-item accessors declare and the engine cannot express at all. Two passing counterfactuals were findings: dropping the untouched side's identity map severed nothing observable because no fixture wired the node's OUTPUT, and disabling the swap-time clamp broke nothing because the fixture never exceeded the target kind's ceiling -- both fixtures were widened until the counterfactual failed.

an axis says which labels it dropped: pinion_chart::fit -- Along / Room / Fitted / FitRule, one derivation that decides which tick labels are drawn and publishes what that cost. Declared `dataviz`. THE GAP WAS IN THE ANALYZER SPEC AND NOT IN THE CENSUS: plane C requires 'high-density label overlap avoidance', R1568 recorded it, R1622's re-audit passed over it, and it lived as prose inside another debt's table with no file of its own -- so grep 'status: open' could not see it. Found by the user asking whether the analyzer work was finished. THE TWO REFERENCES DO DIFFERENT THINGS AND NEITHER IS ENOUGH, both measured from source: the toolkit draws every label and hides the colliders, but only on its VERTICAL axis -- its horizontal one hides a colliding label only when the text has already been elided to '...', and its newer graphs module has no overlap pass at all, one text item per category, elided, always visible. The DCC instead picks the grid STEP from a measured label width so nothing is ever placed too close, which is the better mechanism and only works on an axis with a ladder; its editors have no categorical axis. So this does BOTH, chosen by what the axis is: a ladder axis COARSENS (fewer ticks, no label dropped) and a category axis STRIDES (every tick kept for the grid, some labels dropped, both ends pinned). The ticks and the labels are separated for that reason -- thinning the grid with the labels would take away the slot separators a category axis is read by. MEASURED, NOT MODELLED: the first draft modelled a label's width as its character count times an advance, which was the one axis where this was WORSE than both references; the user asked whether that was the long-term-correct answer and it was not. pinion-core already had the seam -- R1453 §5.36 TextMetrics / measured_text_extent, whose own module doc names count-times-a-cell as the upper bound it retires -- so the fit now measures the real face, in the style the label is about to be painted in, and the model is the declared headless fallback. No new dependency, no purity break, no build-entry signature change, and the shell already seeds the provider. PAST BOTH REFERENCES: the report reaches the scene (label_fit always, labels_omitted only when a label really was left off, label_crowding as a PIXEL measurement when even the coarsest answer fails) and both of them are silent; the ends are pinned where a greedy first-wins scan loses whichever it reaches last; the fallback is declared where a missing measurement elsewhere is a silent zero. FOUR SITES WERE REACHING PAST axis_ticks and drew labels the fit never saw -- bar, boxplot and the candlestick's ordinal arm drew one category label per slot, and bar called nice_ticks directly for its value axis. The first three were found by a derivation test that PASSED VACUOUSLY. hello-category-axis gains a dense 30-endpoint axis because no example in the tree had ever had more categories than room, which is why the defect survived: a forcing consumer that only exercises the easy arity is not forcing the axis. Six counterfactuals, all caught.

a chart is a table to a reader: pinion_a11y::chart projects a chart as table / row / columnheader / rowheader / cell, and BarChart::access_table + ScatterChart::access_table answer it, so what was ONE AccessNode carrying one string is a structure a screen reader navigates. Declared `dataviz`. THE REFERENCES HAVE NOTHING HERE, MEASURED: the toolkit's three charting modules at 6.11 contain no accessibility integration at all between them and a chart view reaches the platform as one scroll-area object; the DCC and the engine have no charting. So for once there was no floor to clear and the shape had to be argued: a TABLE, because that is what a chart's data is (points down, series across), because WAI-ARIA has no chart role and the graphics module's roles are dropped by the platform bridges, and because table/row/cell are roles every screen reader already navigates with commands users already know. Rows are points and columns are series because a chart usually has many points and few series, so the column count -- what a table reader moves ACROSS -- stays small. THE HEADLINE IS THE CONTRAST WITH R1633: that round thins axis labels when there are more of them than room, and this one names every row from the DATA, so the demo asserts 8 labels painted and 30 rows announced in the same frame. Thinning is a fact about pixels and a reader who is not reading pixels is not subject to it; the two reports are consistent rather than in conflict, since labels_omitted says what the PICTURE left off and the table says what the DATA has. The node count is bounded by the chart's own window and by nothing else -- aria-rowcount and aria-setsize state the full extent while the present rows are what was drawn, which is the virtual_list model applied to a chart. The debt file's worry that ten thousand marks would collapse the tree was an untested guess and is not designed around: the tree's rule is that the AT tree exposes what the paint exposes. A cell carries its series name with its value, because a number announced alone has no subject, and resolves its bounds to the MARK it was drawn as so a touch explorer lands on the bar rather than on the chart. Five counterfactuals, all caught. R1634.1 THEN PAID THE HALF OF THE CARRY THAT WAS NEVER A CARRY: the debt file said in its own words that boxplot and candlestick had no structural obstacle and they were deferred anyway. BoxPlotChart::access_table and CandlestickChart::access_table, and the payment validated the abstraction -- both have columns that are NOT series (five summary landmarks, and OHLC), so ChartColumn is redefined as what the chart carries PER POINT rather than as a series. Deferring would have left that resting on one consumer with one column. Two findings fell out: the wire spelling and the announced word are different audiences (SummaryPosition::name vs label), and the word is WHISKER not MINIMUM because a distribution with outliers has values below it, so announcing the minimum states something false to the one reader who cannot check it against the picture.

SCE pin bump (287 commits) plus the gate defect the bump exposed: tools/blast_radius.py reported a radius of ZERO for it. The workspace root Cargo.toml holds the [workspace.dependencies] rev half the tree links against, the lockfile is the resolved answer to it, and vendor/ is the checkout those pins name -- none of the three sits under a member package directory, so owning_packages found no owner and the tool said nothing was affected. Its own docstring asserted that a path under no package cannot break a cargo test, which is true of tools/ and docs/ and false of exactly these. A gate that answers nothing to the change class with the widest reach is worse than no gate, because the zero reads as a clean bill of health. Four selftest cases added, including the counterfactual pair that stops the widening from swallowing every member manifest. No Phase B axis advanced: a dependency pin and a gate repair.

a field that outlived its reason, deleted: ChartStyle::label_advance_px.
