a call must be declared first: the transport now asks the declaration BEFORE it dispatches, on both channels, so a name absent from `$schema` is absent from the wire. Declared `api` -- it is the RPC surface's own contract, the axis whose open items are exactly "what a client may bind to". THE DEBT THIS CLOSES HAD HALF ITS DIAGNOSIS WRONG, and finding that out was the round's first act: R1632 recorded that an External's declared action list "does not reach the wire at all", measured against `rpc/methods` and `scene/snapshot`. Both measurements are true and the conclusion is false -- the list has been on the wire since R825 as the reserved `$schema` introspect PATH, not a `scene/*` method, so a census run on one axis reported absence about something living on another. What was actually missing was the ORDER of two questions: the transport dispatched first and consulted the declaration only to explain a refusal, which left the dangerous direction -- implemented, never declared -- working perfectly and unobservable. R1631's `arrange` was callable and undiscoverable for a full round with `cargo test`, clippy, the demo and the push gate all green, because none of them had two lists to compare. THIS IS THE REFERENCE'S FLOOR, PROVED BY COMPILING IT: a toolkit 6.4.2 class with one `slots:` method and one plain one, driven through the toolkit's meta-object -- invokeMethod ran the declared name and answered true, refused the undeclared one with false and indexOfMethod() == -1, and its 6.11.1 source still emits the same "No such method" from the meta-object's own translation unit. The toolkit reaches the guarantee by codegen; pinion reaches it by gate, because its surfaces are hand-written -- and gets one report out of that the meta-object cannot express, `DeclaredButUnhandled` (the surface published a name and did not answer it), split out of `UnknownInvokePath` so an agent doing the right thing and an agent guessing are no longer told the same word. TURNING THE ORDER AROUND MADE THE TREE SAY WHERE IT WAS WRONG, which is the answer the debt file said was impossible from source text: 123 undeclared or mis-declared actions (56 never declared, 67 declared as READ slots and dispatched as verbs -- `$schema` saying "query me" about names only `invoke` answers), plus 2 on the read channel, one of them `pinion_widget_paint::dock`'s `lifecycle` whose own doc calls it "surfaced as scene-as-data via query(lifecycle) (§2 #7)". `pinion-audio`'s two Externals had their ENTIRE invoke surface undeclared while the type doc described all ten verbs in prose. Five names carried BOTH channels at one address (bump/boost/restamp/dense/focus_region) and a field holds one channel, so whichever was declared hid the other -- split into a tally and a verb, which is what the reference does too (a property and its setX() are different meta-object namespaces). Three surfaces hand-copied an upstream declaration and were moved to `SchemaField::concat`; `hello-tab-reorder`'s copy had already lost `send` and demoted `move` and `grab_cancel` to reads. THE SOURCE CENSUS FAILED THREE TIMES and what caught each miss is recorded: it read only the first match, then missed tuple-pattern arms (`("bump", Int(n)) =>`, found by a DEMO dying), then missed `if path == "..."`. The final method was to over-report every string literal in an invoke body and classify by hand -- and the general lesson is that the wire gate RETIRES the census, because an undeclared action now dies in its own demo. Eight counterfactuals, 8/8 caught after the first run of CF-7 PASSED and was a finding: nothing anywhere asserted a declared read reaches the wire, because every `lifecycle` assertion in the tree calls the trait directly. The test written to fix that found three more mis-declarations in dock on its first run, and its first oracle ("every declared read answers") had to be replaced -- it reported fourteen text_field paths that answer None because the widget is UNBOUND, which is a fixture that cannot discriminate; asking the surface's own dispatch instead needs no binding and is exact.

an action says what it takes: ArgForm (Undeclared / Path / Nullary / Scalar / Object / Delimited) plus SchemaField::action_with plus SchemaArg::optional plus ArgDomain::OneOf, so a declared verb carries its argument grammar and not only its name. Declared `api` -- it is the same RPC contract axis R1637 advanced, and this is the half R1637 left unsaid. THE ROUND STARTS FROM BEING BEHIND THE REFERENCE, which is rare enough to say plainly: a meta-method publishes each parameter's name and type and generates that list from the signature, while pinion published `{"path": "arrange", "channel": "invoke"}` and nothing else -- 45 of 45 actions on one surface, measured over the wire at R1637. An agent could discover a verb existed and still had to read our source to call it. SILENCE IS AN ARM, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S CENTRAL DECISION. 487 actions are declared in this tree and the overwhelming majority take an argument nothing describes, so making an empty `args` mean "takes nothing" would have converted every one of them into an affirmative false statement -- the error direction R1602 records as the expensive one, because a wrong `have` inflates silently while a wrong `absent` self-corrects. `Undeclared` publishes NO `args` key at all and `Nullary` publishes an empty list, so a client can tell "has not said" from "takes nothing". The reference cannot represent the first state at all, because a generated parameter list is always a claim. PAST THE REFERENCE IN TWO PLACES: an argument says where its values COME FROM rather than only its type -- `OneOf` for a closed vocabulary and `ValuesOf` for a live path on the same surface -- where a meta-method gives a type name and constrains only enum-typed parameters through its meta-enum; and `optional` marks the segments a delimited payload may elide, with the invariant that they must be a SUFFIX, which is forced by the only form that can elide anything. EVERY CLOSED VOCABULARY IS PROJECTED FROM ITS DEFINITION, NOT WRITTEN OUT: `Axis::WIRE_NAMES`, `Edge::WIRE_NAMES`, `ArrangePass::WIRE_NAMES` and `VoicePolicy::WIRE_NAMES` are const-evaluated from each type's own `ALL` through its own `name()` / `as_wire()`, and `ALL`'s length is the `VariantCensus` arm count -- so a new variant is a BUILD failure rather than a vocabulary quietly one short on the wire. That projection is what makes a literal domain defensible at all; a hand-written list would be exactly the disconnected census R1630 exists to end, and the `ArgDomain` doc now states the line between a model-derived bound (never a literal) and a code-derived vocabulary (a literal, projected). ARRANGEPASS IS THE CRATE LIFT THIS FORCED: R1631 turned the reference's eleven commands into an axis, an edge and a gap and left the fourth parameter -- WHICH pass -- as four string literals matched at the call site, which is the same shape one level up. It is now a value with `ALL` / `name` / `from_wire` / `tail`, and the example dispatches through it. THE WIRE RENDER IS DERIVED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, which closed a latent defect in the same edit: `$schema` was two hand-written shapes and the one carrying `args` had silently dropped `channel`. Nothing had noticed because no constructor could produce a field that was both parametric and an action, so the arm had no inhabitants -- `action_with` gives it inhabitants, and an action that said what it takes would have rendered as a path a client may read. A BLANKET SUBSTITUTION WAS TRIED AND REVERTED, and the reason is the round's sharpest lesson: attaching the composite send grammar to all 67 `send` declarations produced FALSE CLAIMS, because `send` is at least four different grammars under one name (20 composite, 11 bare event name, 6 accepting both, 15 hand-rolled). The discriminator that let it through was "does the file mention `split_send_payload`" and the mention in `pinion-audio` was a DOC COMMENT -- the third time this session a text census read something that was not code. The grammar is now declared once in `composite_tag::SEND_ARGS` and pointed at by the 24 declarations whose decoder was verified by CALL SITE; the other 43 stay silent, and the four-grammar collision is registered rather than papered over. THE SUFFIX INVARIANT CAUGHT ITS AUTHOR ON ITS FIRST RUN: `key` was declared optional because the bare-target wire is `":<Event>:<token>"`, and that segment is present-and-EMPTY rather than elided, so it made `event` follow an optional argument. Eight counterfactuals, 8/8 caught -- one had to be re-authored because removing a line left an unused binding and so did not compile, which the driver reports as testing nothing. A demo that builds `arrange`'s payload OUT OF THE SCHEMA -- separator, segment order and vocabularies all read off the wire -- and lands all eight published combinations, refuses two unpublished values by name, and then follows an argument's declared `values_path` on the audio surface to a live voice id.

a widget publishes the events it accepts: `#[derive(WidgetEventName)]` emits DRIVABLE_NAMES as a const projected from the EXTERNALLY_DRIVABLE_EVENTS the statechart codegen already emits, and the eleven bare-event `send` declarations point their argument's domain at it. Declared `api` -- the same RPC contract axis as R1637 and R1638, closing the first of the three choices the send-collision debt named. THE COMMONEST ACTION IN THE TREE WAS THE LEAST DESCRIBED. R1638 gave an action an argument grammar and could describe none of these: the legal names are per widget and existed only as a runtime `Vec`, reachable when a refusal was being worded and nowhere a schema could point at. So the vocabulary was discoverable ONLY BY GETTING IT WRONG -- R1564 made the refusal name the accepted set, which is a good refusal and a poor contract, because it asks an agent to make a call it expects to fail before it can make one it expects to succeed. A TRAIT METHOD CANNOT BE CONST, which is the whole reason this needed the derive rather than a helper: an argument's domain is a `&'static [&'static str]` evaluated at compile time, and `as_name` is a trait method. So the macro emits the arms TWICE -- once as the trait's `as_name` and once as an inherent `const fn wire_name` -- which is duplication a generator does and an author never sees, and the const is then folded out of the codegen's own drivable list. The set a client reads, the set a refusal advertises and the set `from_name` admits are one list BY CONSTRUCTION. INTERNAL EVENTS STAY UNFORGEABLE, and that is what makes publishing safe: the projection is over the DRIVABLE const, not the variant list, so a chart-raised `ButtonActivate` is absent from the published set and refused on the wire. A schema reader who assumed every event of the machine was callable would have been wrong, and the demo asserts both halves. THE SIX DUAL-GRAMMAR SURFACES WERE DECIDED RATHER THAN LEFT: datepicker, disclosure_group, listbox, radio_group, table and text_field decode a composite payload AND fall back to a bare event, and `ArgForm` has no union arm. It deliberately gains none -- a declaration states what a client SHOULD send, and a shorthand the surface also accepts is a convenience rather than a contract, so the composite form is declared because it is the one that stays true if the shorthand is retired. Same call `pinion_audio::play` made for its bare-string form; the union question is left where it belongs, in the debt that owns the collision. A CONSTRUCTOR COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AND THAT IS RECORDED: `SchemaField::send_event(returns, names)` was drafted and removed, because a `const fn` cannot build the `&'static [SchemaArg]` a field needs out of its own parameter -- a function argument is not promotable. The helper is therefore at the ARGUMENT level (`SchemaArg::event`) and the call site writes the one-element slice in a `const` block, which is where promotion is legal. The reason is in the doc so the next round does not re-derive it. A catalog walk now refuses to let a `send` be silent (and refuses an empty vocabulary, which is the shape a widget whose chart drives nothing externally would publish); it found the two dual-grammar surfaces in the catalog on its first run. Four counterfactuals, 4/4 caught. A demo that drives TWO different widgets -- one example would pass against a shared global list -- plays every published name through the real wire, checks that a refusal still teaches the set, and asserts the composite surfaces declare four segments and which of them may be elided.

the catalog walk is every widget surface, and its escape hatch is not free: the channel checks R1637-R1639 built now construct all THIRTY-NINE `ExternalIntrospect` impls in pinion-core's widget directory rather than the nineteen whose constructors took no arguments, and a completeness gate holds the list to the source. Declared `api` -- these are the gates that keep the RPC contract true, and a gate covering half its population while reporting a pass is the shape this round removes. THE DENOMINATOR WAS STATED NOWHERE, which is what made the gap invisible: the walk built what was easy to build, passed, and read as coverage. Measured when the debt was registered: 19 of 39, with `TableExternal`, `ListBoxExternal`, `RadioGroupExternal` and `ToolbarExternal` -- four large composite-send surfaces -- among the twenty nobody had ever checked. Widening it found a real mis-declared channel in the first run (`ColumnResizeExternal`'s `send` was declared a READ slot and has always been dispatched through `split_send_payload`), which is the same hit rate the walk had on its first run against dock. THE ORACLE HAD A HOLE AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL CLOSED IT. The channel check asked "does the surface's `invoke` answer this declared read with anything other than UnknownPath", and a surface that declines EVERY name with one stated sentence answers that yes for names it has never heard of: `ButtonStateSnapshot` and `ToggleStateSnapshot` refuse uniformly ("this surface is a read-only copy; drive the live button external instead"), and three of their declared reads were reported as mis-declared channels on the first widened run. The walk now probes an invented name first and compares the shapes -- a surface that answers a name it does not know the same way it answers a declared one is telling us nothing about either. Three false positives out, one true positive left. A FUZZY COMPARISON INSIDE A COMPLETENESS GATE IS ITS OWN FAILURE MODE: the first draft matched a snake_case catalog label against the type name by lowercasing and dropping underscores, and four entries that WERE in the catalog came back unaccounted (`row_dissect` against `RowDissectionExternal`). The labels are now the type names and the comparison is an exact set difference. AND THE ESCAPE HATCH IS NOT FREE -- a counterfactual adding a reason-less exclusion PASSED against the first draft, making the gate's own opt-out the cheapest way through it. An exclusion must now state a reason of real length AND name a type that is actually in the source, so a stale exclusion cannot silently shrink the denominator either. The source scan follows R1605 rather than counting: it collects names and every name must be in the catalog or in the stated exclusions, so a mis-parse surfaces as an unaccounted NAME a reader can act on rather than as a number that happens to match -- which matters because this session burned three times on text censuses that read a comment, a tuple pattern, and only the first match. Four counterfactuals, 4/4 caught after two were re-authored: one did not compile (removing a catalog entry orphaned its import, and the driver reports that as testing nothing) and one was the finding above. 32 demos over the surfaces whose declarations moved, all pass.

a number and its unit sit on one line: AlignItems::Baseline plus LetterSpacing { Normal, PxX100, EmX1000 } plus the first written statement of which whitespace a measured box contains. Declared `text` -- letter spacing is a character format property and the R1560 audit records the character half as unchanged since R1546; the baseline work is the layout primitive that half of a type scale is useless without. THE ROUND IS A CONSUMER REPORT, and the first thing it cost was a design that was already wrong. A field report from a repo that git-rev-pins pinion ported a production design system to an all-Korean product UI and reported three things; two of them were mis-scoped by ME before the reference was read, and the user asking whether the reference had been compared is what caught it. THE FIRST MIS-SCOPE: the report said letter_spacing: i32 cannot hold four of its five tracking values (-1.5 / -0.5 / -0.3 / +1.5 px; only -1 fit) and pointed at `as f32` downstream as proof nothing blocked a float. True, and the repair is not a float -- TextStyle derives Eq + Hash and that participates in the 5.16 paint-fragment cache key, so a float takes both away. Fixed point keeps them. But precision was only the reported symptom: the reference toolkit's font takes a spacing MODE beside the value -- a percentage of each glyph's own natural advance, or an absolute length -- so spacing being specifiable RELATIVE TO THE FONT is the existence floor, and a scale restated per size is what a scale exists to avoid. So the field is now a type shaped like LineHeight one type above it -- the same either-or, absolute device units or a fraction of the font -- rather than the finer i32 I had already written and tested. Em-relative rather than the reference's advance-relative, stated as a deliberate difference: parley takes ONE absolute per-cluster spacing, so an advance-proportional form cannot be resolved to a single number, and that is registered rather than glossed. Thousandths not hundredths because tracking lives at 0.01-0.1 em where two digits quantise a scale coarser than its own values. THE SECOND MIS-SCOPE, AND THE ROUND'S SHARPEST FINDING: baseline alignment looks like a missing enum arm and mapping AlignItems::Baseline to TaffyAlign::Baseline would have shipped a variant that MOVES NOTHING. taffy 0.7.7 types its measure callback FnOnce(..) -> Size<f32> with no channel for a baseline, so every measured leaf returns first_baselines: Point::NONE and flexbox does baseline.unwrap_or(height) -- which for a text leaf IS the box's bottom edge. Measured, not read: the naive mapping places the pair at exactly End's relative offset (both 53px), and the test says the baselines are still 10px apart. That is the wrong-`have` direction R1602 names as the expensive one, and it was one line away. What ships instead computes each participant's baseline BEFORE layout and injects the difference as taffy margin.top, so the row's own height is the layout engine's answer about the shifted children rather than a correction applied after it -- a test asserts the row still contains what it moved. TextBox gains baseline: Option<f32> for the same reason it gained line_count at R1344, a fact only the measure knows; Option rather than a synthesized fallback so a measure that reports nothing takes its item OUT of the alignment visibly instead of aligning every row slightly wrong. The 5.37 self-hosted engine reports the SAME LineBoxMetrics::baseline_px its paint arm draws on. Non-text items keep Start where CSS synthesizes from the bottom margin edge, and that boundary is documented as a boundary: a synthesized baseline needs a laid-out height, which is exactly what computing before layout does not have. THE THIRD OBSERVATION WAS ONE SYMPTOM WITH TWO CAUSES and the report had merged them. Trailing whitespace reproduces on the first run -- the intrinsic measure is parley's width(), documented as "excluding the width of trailing whitespace" -- and LEADING whitespace does not; it is measured. A fix aimed at full_width() would have closed one half of what was filed as one thing. The choice is correct (CSS removes a flex item's trailing whitespace) and was written down nowhere, so it is now a test plus the paragraph on TextNode that sends a reader to `runs` BEFORE they reach for two adjacent nodes -- the report's own framing was that runs' documentation is excellent to someone who already found runs. Two nits closed the same way: PathPoint / Stroke name their constructors, because non_exhaustive rejects a struct literal and rustc's E0639 does not say what to call instead; and WidgetCore's trait doc now says #[widget] exists, since 57 examples use it and the consumer hand-wrote the impl and filed the required event_name/title pair as missing defaults -- it HAS them, the type leading you there did not say so. Two counterfactuals, 2/2 caught, one of them re-authored because deleting the call left dead functions and so did not compile, which tests nothing. Four debts registered, two of them existence-floor gaps this round surfaced and did not close (no word_spacing at all, though CSS, the reference and parley all have it; and advance-relative tracking, blocked upstream).

a conditional argument declares its cases: ArgDomain::OneOfWith plus ArgCase, so an argument whose value decides the REST of the call says so, and the two verbs that need it (arrange, item) are declared from the model own answers. Declared api -- the same RPC contract axis R1637-R1640 advanced, and the round also re-judges api 65 to 72 and text 90 to 92, both STALE at the push gate. THE DECLARATION WAS NOT SILENT, IT WAS WRONG. R1638 described arrange third segment as one slot, string domain open optional, which is the only sentence a flat positional argument list can produce about a segment that is a closed edge vocabulary after align, an integer after stack, and ABSENT after distribute and straighten. Measured over the wire before the fix: that declaration admits nine calls and the dispatcher refuses three of them (align:horizontal elided, align:horizontal:17, stack:horizontal:start) and ACCEPTS AND SILENTLY IGNORES a fourth (distribute:horizontal:start). Silence would have been honest; that carried a schema authority, which is the wrong-have direction R1602 names as the expensive one. And item could not have been fixed by a flat list at any price: add:in:1, remove:in:0 and move:in:2:0 are three different ARITIES, so no positional list describes them, and item published no args at all. THE CASE TABLE HANGS OFF THE DISCRIMINANT for R1593 reason, restated: which values may I pass and what does that value then require are ONE fact, and a declaration that splits them lets them drift, exactly as link legality and link conversion became one declaration so may I draw this and what arrives if I do could not disagree. PAST THE REFERENCE, AND THE REFERENCE PROVES ITS OWN CEILING: a meta-method parameter list is generated from one C++ signature, so a conditional argument there has to become SEPARATE METHODS -- which is what the toolkit does, and R1631 folded exactly those eleven alignment command names into parameters. Its one concession is the Cloned attribute, the synthetic shorter overloads a default argument generates, which enumerates arities and cannot say two of them belong to different values of one parameter. So a client there discovers seven unrelated verb names; here it discovers two verbs and seven cases, which is the same information plus the fact that they are two operations. THE TABLE IS PROJECTED AND THE PROJECTION IS GATED AT COMPILE TIME. ArrangePass::tail and the new ItemEdit::tail answer what a verb reads after its shared segments, each tail answers required, and the case arrays are const loops over ALL -- so a new pass or edit cannot arrive without a case. What cannot be projected is the SchemaArg itself, because pinion-node-graph is pure data and must not depend on the framework to name one, so the argument name, type and vocabulary are spelled at the declaration and a const assertion (ArgCase::adds) holds the pair to the model facts: swapping which tail may be elided is now error[E0080] by name, not a schema that lies. THE RULE IS ONE DEFINITION WITH THREE CALLERS: SchemaField::conditional_defect refuses two discriminants, an optional discriminant, a shadowed argument name, an expansion that puts an optional before a required, and a nested case table -- the last forbidden not because the append rule breaks down but because an unexercised wire shape is a claim no client has been held to. Seven unit tests drive it, one per arm plus a legal control, because a checker that refused everything would pass every refusal test. THE GATE STATES ITS DENOMINATOR: no pinion-core widget declares a case table, so the workspace walk asserts the INHABITANT COUNT IS ZERO rather than reporting no defects over an empty population -- R1640 finding applied to the gate written the round after it. A SIDE-EFFECT FINDING, SAME CLASS ONE SEGMENT ALONG: item side was declared as the closed pair in and out, but which side ANSWERS is the selected node kind business, so the pair advertised calls the surface refuses. It now points at a live path (item_sides) that empties when no call is well formed. 13 counterfactuals: 5 caught by unit tests, 2 caught by the const build gate and therefore scored BROKEN by the harness (debt-counterfactual-cannot-score-a-build-gate, second and third instances -- confirmed by hand that the E0080 message is the assertion own), and 6 by the demo after CF-10 PASSED and was a real fixture gap, since nothing had ever selected two nodes and read the live domain. A 40-plus-assertion demo builds every call the declaration admits from the wire alone -- separator, segment order, per-case arguments, and both the present and elided forms of anything optional -- lands all 20 of them, and refuses eleven calls the declaration excludes including the one that used to be accepted and ignored. R1638, R1631, R1632, R1637 and R1639 demos re-pass, R1638 own payload builder rewritten to read the case table since that is what it claims to do.

the declaration gate reaches every surface: paint_catalog plus every_catalog plus a two-area completeness scan close debt-the-declaration-walk-reaches-one-crate, and the nine demos R1637 left red in CI are green. Declared api -- the same RPC contract axis R1637-R1642 advanced, and this is the round that pays its unpaid bill. STOP-THE-LINE, AND THE RED WAS SIX ROUNDS OLD. CI had failed on every push since R1640 and the sweep named nine demos; all nine reproduce locally and deterministically, so none is a flake. Every one is R1637 declaration gate firing on a surface no local gate can see, in three distinct kinds. ClickRouter::click had been declared with SchemaField::new -- a READ -- since R683.C, while invoke is the only thing that answers it and query returns None, so the declaration was wrong in BOTH directions at once; three demos refused with PathIsAReadSlot. hello-node-flow declared twenty-one reads and ZERO actions while act dispatches ten verbs, the pinion-audio shape R1637 found, in an example R1637 source census could not reach because the binding landed at R1599/R1600 and the census was a hand classification of invoke-body string literals; two demos refused with UnknownInvokePath. And four demos over hello-answer-origin walk every declared slot through query, which R1637 made false for an action. THE FOURTH KIND IS THE SHARPEST: that walker exists FIVE times, and R1641.6 repaired the fifth copy -- a Rust unit test -- while its own blast-radius note read the two sibling UNIT walks and not these four. The shared definition was not missing either: assert_declared_channels_are_true has been in rpc_verify since R1566, seventy-seven rounds, used by exactly one demo. So the duplication was not for want of an abstraction, it was for want of a POINTER to one, and what R1643 adds is the small piece those four walks each need -- declared_read_paths, the filter -- rather than a whole-surface assertion they would have to be rewritten around. WIDENING PARTIALLY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASS. The first wiring routed two of the three channel checks at every_catalog and the third still iterated catalog -- and the third was precisely the one whose oracle catches ClickRouter. Counterfactual CF-1 found it: the case that was supposed to prove the widening PASSED, which is the finding, and the fix made it CAUGHT. THE WIDENED WALK THEN FOUND A REAL MIS-DECLARATION ON ITS FIRST RUN: SplitterExternal.send is also declared READ and also dispatched by invoke -- the same hit rate the walk had on dock (3 on its first run) and on the 39-widget widening (1). Repaying it published PointerWireEvent::ALL and WIRE_NAMES, projected from the enum through a const spelling of as_wire_name, because the surface accepts exactly the five names from_wire_name admits and had no way to say so. A FOURTH COPY OF THE ARM LIST WENT WITH IT: the round-trip test in input.rs carried its own hand-written five-element array, so a sixth event would have left the one place that checks the round trip silently short. AND THE RATCHET ITSELF HAS A HOLE, found by counterfactual and registered: variant_census(all) holds ALL LENGTH to the arm count and cannot see an arm written TWICE. Replacing Cancel with a second Leave keeps the length right, publishes PointerLeave twice, loses PointerCancel entirely, and left the whole workspace suite green -- including the round-trip test written in this very round, because walking ALL and asking from_wire_name(WIRE_NAMES[i]) == ALL[i] is satisfied by the duplicate. R1630 had already recorded the argument that closes it (total plus surjective plus equal cardinality implies injective) and the test had only the third term; a distinct-set check supplies the second. Registered as a general debt because every ALL in this tree has the same hole and this round closed one. THE COMPLETENESS GATE IS PER AREA, NOT POOLED: each source name is compared against ITS OWN area catalog, so a fat catalog cannot account for a starved one. 8 counterfactuals across three gate scopings, and the scoping itself taught something: CF-5 PASSED against a gate that excluded pinion-core, the crate holding the guard it was testing -- the harness own rule 2 (a scoped gate cannot say NOTHING catches a break) applies to package selection and not only to test filters. Final: 6/6 caught, the two example-side cases confirmed against a demo-inclusive gate because the walk deliberately does not reach examples and the demo is what gates them.

a run can be stopped, stepped and watched: pinion-node-graph::debug -- Breakpoints, Watches, Session, Timeline, Paused, and Command::STRIDES as the 2x3 product of Direction and Stride. Declared `dcc` -- the node-graph third of that axis, and it closes the DEBUGGING cluster the R1604 judgment names among the engine's eight (breakpoints 5, watches 2, stepping): the census's engine half moves 51% -> 62% and its tree-debugger command list 2/9 -> 9/9. THE DESIGN IS ONE SENTENCE: A BREAKPOINT CANNOT CHANGE THE RUN. The debugger suspends nothing. It computes the whole run once, WITHOUT REFERENCE TO ANY BREAKPOINT, and then moves about inside it -- so the property is structural rather than promised, and it is bought by R1600's decision that state is a delay and nothing else, which makes a run a pure function of the document and the registers. Nothing weaker would do: a debugger that halts a running machine observes a DIFFERENT execution from the one the program has without it, and reverse stepping then has to replay recorded frames -- which is exactly why the reference's tree debugger has CurrentValues and SavedValues as two commands over two data sources. Here they are one object, asserted: the readings are identical at two positions while the trace prefix is not. FIVE STEPPING COMMANDS ARE TWO WORDS. Direction x Stride is six, Command::STRIDES is that product computed at compile time (array length is the product, the fill is positional, an unfilled cell is a const panic), and the sixth cell -- stepping back OUT -- is not a feature added on top but the one the reference's naming left unwritten. The R1643 hole is closed by construction here rather than by a length check. OUT IS THE ONE STRIDE THAT DOES NOT INVERT, and that is the operation rather than a defect: leaving a frame is precisely forgetting which frame you were in. Asserted over every position and every stride -- into is an exact bijection, over inverts when it stayed in its frame, and all three bracket. AN OCCURRENCE IS PART OF THE ADDRESS: a NodeSite and a PortSite carry Occurrence::{Any, At}, so 'stop the second time through this subgraph' is a thing to say. The reference cannot express it at all -- it expands a macro into a copy per use before anything runs. A MARK THAT COULD NEVER FIRE IS REFUSED, checked at the document for the reason Document::force is (R1601.1): only the document knows the node has no control port (pure -- pulled, never run) or is a group instance (takes no turn of its own). A silently inert mark reads as a mark that never fired. AND A MARK THAT OUTLIVES WHAT IT MARKED IS NAMED, NOT DROPPED, with the reason, on the same channel -- the reference asks the same question one breakpoint at a time and answers bool. A READING IS PER OCCURRENCE, NOT PER STEP, and that is a consequence rather than a simplification: a port's value is a pure function of the document and the registers, so within one run it cannot differ between two moments; what it differs between is instances. It reports ran_at, because a value off the trace (a pure node) and a value the run never reached look alike and are not. 23 census rows closed with 22 proofs (schema::ClearPinWatch cites the graph editor's, one mechanism answering two rows). 13 counterfactuals, 13/13 caught -- two re-authored because the first draft did not compile and therefore tested nothing, and one of those was a BUILD gate catching the break (removing the Elsewhere arm's only constructor makes the variant dead code), which is debt-counterfactual-cannot-score-a-build-gate's fourth instance. A 48-assertion demo drives the whole surface. NO CENSUS ROW MOVES: neither reference has an observed layer, their graphs are wholly authored, so this axis is the spec's rather than theirs -- stated because a round that advances a capability and moves no number looks like one that did nothing.

a card says what it is showing, and the analyzer shell is assembled by hand. The pair that justifies six arms rather than one Error is denied/opaque: both render as 'no content' and they are opposite, so a shell with one arm offers 'request access' on a link no permission can open. remedy returns Option so the absence of a problem, a remedy, and a needed remedy that does not exist are three answers (R1610). Measured on the toolkit at 6.11: NO content-state concept exists on any panel or view class, and its item views have no placeholder at all. CardChrome is a set in one canonical layout order, so two applications spelling their definitions differently lay out identically, and the set is ENFORCED ON THE WIRE -- an affordance a card does not offer is refused by name, because hiding a button leaves an agent able to do what the screen says is impossible. MAXIMISE HANDS BACK THE WAY HOME AS A #[must_use] VALUE: TileGrid::maximize returns Maximized, which IS the previous arrangement, so there is no copy on the side to be clobbered by a second maximise or dropped by a preset load. THE SHELL IS OPERATED BY HAND, not only over the wire (user directive): press the chips, press the header affordances, drag a card to rearrange, press an actionable remedy, and a keymap the window prints along its own bottom edge and publishes on the wire. A real press and a scripted one reach ONE set of handlers -- the router's pointer_move and PointerDown/PointerUp, the wire's point and key -- so there is no automation surface that can drift from what a hand does. Controls fire on RELEASE over the same target, and a cancel drops the latch WITHOUT performing it. THE GEOMETRY IS ONE THING, READ BY BOTH THE PAINTER AND THE HIT TEST, and the demo sweeps the window in both directions to keep it so: every name the hit test produces must be a tag the scene painted, and every painted control must be pressable at the centre of its painted rectangle. THE SECOND DIRECTION WAS MISSING AND A COUNTERFACTUAL PROVED IT -- adding it immediately found that this file painted every card's contents at TWICE their intended offset, because children of an absolutely-positioned container are placed relative to IT and the first draft wrote them in window coordinates. a painted surface says what a pointer cannot reach: pinion_runtime::pointer_reach plus scene/pointer_reach plus a boot gate every demo pays, and the gate found a second whole app dead to a real mouse on its first run. Declared `none` -- this round builds an instrument and pays a defect with it; claiming an axis for that would be the hand-adjustment these ledgers exist to stop, and the repair it made lands on hello-tile-dashboard, whose own rounds (R1607-R1609) declared `none` for the same reason. THE ROUND EXISTS BECAUSE TWO FACTS WERE BEING ASSERTED AS ONE. `scene/click`, `invoke` and `send` reach a widget's handler BY NAME; a mouse reaches it BY POSITION through the router, which resolves the deepest tagged node under the cursor and looks that tag's primary half up as an External -- and returns SILENTLY when the lookup fails. So a screen can be completely dead to a hand while every scripted assertion about it passes. Measured twice before anything checked it (R1497 lost 100% of the clicks on two header cells; R1649.1 found a whole shell dead behind 118 passing assertions) and a THIRD time by this gate: hello-tile-dashboard had been dead since R1608, whose changelog says 'the model's claim gets a cursor'. Proven with scene/drag -- UNCHANGED under a router-driven drag, MOVED under invoke. THE REPAIR WAS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE: pointer_transparent takes the whole subtree out of the hit test and the grip ring's eight resize cursors are declared inside it, so the answer is the idiom the tree already had -- a COMPOSITE tag (dashboard#card.loss), plus CaptureNormalize::Primary (without it the cursor arrives as a fraction of the grabbed CARD and every drag lands elsewhere) plus decoding the router's composite send payload (without it the input finally arrived and the board still did nothing). THE VERDICT AND THE CENSUS ARE TWO HALVES AND THE SWEEP TAUGHT WHICH IS WHICH: `shadows` reports every tag intercepting a widget's input, which a tagged container legitimately does in its own gaps, and `unreachable` reports a widget whose own centre NO widget answers. The first draft asked whether the widget answered for ITSELF and flagged four containers immediately -- a row over its tree and a cell over its grid are ordinary nesting. Measured over 148 examples that boot with a GPU surface: 14 had a widget nobody can press. Two were repaired here (a label that had grown over its own badge, a status message region that had grown over its bar) and the other 12 are a BUDGET FILE, the ratchet shape R1611 used for 7,999 reference-name occurrences, because a gate that fails everything on day one is a gate somebody switches off. THE WALK IS THE PRIMITIVE 78 TEST FILES HAD BEEN WRITING THEMSELVES: Scene::for_each_node with child_nodes exhaustive over the node-kind census, so a new kind cannot join the tree while every traversal steps over it, and NodeVisit carries the ancestor chain because a path cannot -- a Scroll is path-transparent, so depth is not the segment count. THE GATE'S FIRST SWEEP FOUND A DEFECT IN THE GATE: raising from __enter__ leaks the subprocess, because `with` only calls __exit__ for an __enter__ that RETURNED, and 14 refusals left 14 binaries holding GPU contexts until the next launch died with 'Not enough memory left' instead of its own verdict -- R1570.3's class, reproduced by the thing written to prevent a different one. AND THE REFERENCE CLAIMS GET A METER: tools/reference_surface.py re-derives what this project asserts about the reference toolkit, with the parsed member count PINNED, because an absence proved by search is worth nothing -- a pattern matching nothing and a parse finding nothing look identical. Three claims, re-derived: the transparency attribute exists (so our declaration matches the floor), and of the base widget class's 280 declared members none answers the aggregate reachability question or says whether a press will be acted on. 12 counterfactuals, 12 caught after THREE were findings -- nothing asserted the shadow names the NEAREST widget, nothing could fail when the composite tags were reverted, and the normalisation choice was invisible to cargo and needed a demo-inclusive gate. Also cleared: the two things the push gate demanded of this round -- the catalog axis re-judged 95 to 96, and the measurement is the point (one of the five named absent widget kinds, a key-sequence editor, landed at R1569, the round BEFORE the judgment that called it missing, so that gap has been four kinds for eighty rounds) and hello-analyzer-shell filed on the axis its artifact belongs to.

the node inspector is a widget, and the reference's screen A is assembled on it. Declared `catalog` -- pinion_widget_paint::config_form is a new widget with a crate home, and the analysis-tool census's must-have row for it (lab.t0.2) had scored `gap` since R1646 for want of anywhere to live. THE ROUND EXISTS BECAUSE R1650 BUILT HALF OF IT: it gave the MODEL a home and left it with no painter and no consumer, which is the shape R1646 measured and named -- no crate held a property grid, so an application that wanted one copied an example. THE FLOOR WAS MEASURED, NOT READ. The mature toolkit at 6.11 was built from source and a three-row form was RUN through it, because R1557 recorded three doc statements out of three being false. Its row-wrap policy has three settings and the third is derived per row (320px box: all three rows stay beside their labels; 140px box: only the row whose label measures 153px moves); its field-growth policy is 108px at the size hint against 161px when allowed to grow; hiding the middle of three rows took the form 159px -> 104px with the row count unchanged. All three are reproduced (RowWrap, FieldGrowth, ConfigField::hidden). TWO MEASURED FINDINGS CORRECTED CLAIMS THIS ROUND WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE WRITTEN: its controls DO carry an edited flag, so the missing half is not dirtiness; and its label-to-control accessible relation is NOT automatic -- passing a label the application owns leaves the relation unset, so a form assembled the way an application assembles one has controls with no accessible name at all. Here the relation is derived from the same geometry the paint came from, through describedby_region (its 4th consumer). WHAT THE FLOOR HAS NO VOCABULARY FOR, and why this is a type rather than a layout: across the five classes a settings form is built from, 105 distinct declared properties, and NOT ONE is about whether an edit reaches the running program; its per-field verdict has three values and the middle one means keep typing -- measured, an integer control bounded 0..=65535 answers that same middle value for the empty string and for 70000, so `not finished` and `out of range` are one answer and neither is `wrong, and the program will start anyway`; and the mapping between a form and the settings it edits is written by hand TWICE, once to load and once to save, with nothing checking the two agree. THE DEFECT LIST IS NOW DERIVED rather than handed in (R1650 took it as an argument, which let a screen show a clean gate over a form holding an unparseable value), FieldType is six arms chosen from what one real inspector needs rather than from a widget catalogue, and ConfigForm::document / ConfigForm::adopt are ONE mapping with a round-trip law over it: document -> form -> document is identity, a path the form has no row for is NAMED rather than dropped, and a refused document does not half-apply. THE THEME GAINED A WARNING TIER, argued rather than assumed: this project follows Material 3's role set everywhere else and M3 has an error tier and no warning tier, but ConfigDefect's arms differ in exactly one way -- whether the defect blocks -- and a palette with one alarm tone can only paint half of that vocabulary. Two roles, not four, because nothing fills a warning CONTAINER yet. THE SPECIFICATION IS A VALUE: examples/hello-node-lab/src/spec.rs holds the reference screen as a table (panes and widths, palette groups, the opening graph's nodes and positions, the inspector's rows and their applies-scopes), main.rs is written AGAINST it, and the table is published on the wire so the demo asserts the painted scene against it IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- an element the screen is missing and an element the screen invented are both failures. The forward direction checks 48+ declared elements; the backward direction accounts for all 136 painted tags. A cross-check between the table and the taxonomy caught a drift the same session (the table said a responder cannot be dialled; it answers queries, so it must be). THE GRAPH IS THE CRATE'S: pinion_node_graph::Document holds the nodes, frames and links, so a link the model cannot hold is refused BY THE CRATE and named. That forced a real modelling question -- the reference's router shows FOUR inbound links on ONE pin, and a dataflow value input holds one wire because a value has one source. The crate derives multiplicity from the flow and offers no many-to-one value input, which is RIGHT for a value, so the many-ness is expressed the way the crate expresses it: the accept port is a variadic RUN (R1632), one port per link, drawn as one pin because a person authoring a topology is not choosing which slot to land in. TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY DRIVING IT rather than by reasoning. The demo found that a form edit changed the gate on the wire and left the screen showing the old row -- the document and the forms sit behind RefCells (a Signal over either would clone the whole graph per read) and the reactive substrate cannot see through them, so every mutation now bumps a revision the view reads. The REAL POINTER run found that a node added from the palette never reached the canvas, because the card list was derived from the specification table rather than from the document: the specification says what the screen OPENS with, and a screen that could only ever draw that is a picture. Both are stated in the code at the site rather than in a note. Verified: 14 example tests, 21 config-form model tests, 8 painter tests, a 14-section demo (all panes, both completeness directions, 40 painted controls each answering a press at the centre of the rectangle they were painted in, all four advertised gestures), and a REAL MOUSE through xdotool over a mapped window driving five separate controls including a framework-painted form row.
